flashcards.detail: A template such as CORP-%RAND:5% gives unique, predictable names without scripts. The name has to fit in 15 characters after the macros expand, so a long prefix plus %SERIAL% can fail on devices with long serial numbers.

flashcards.front: Choosing Autopilot deployment profiles or device preparation policies
flashcards.back: Device preparation needs no hardware hash registration, supports Microsoft Entra join only, offers user-driven and automatic modes, and delivers up to 25 essential apps and 10 scripts during OOBE. Classic profiles need device registration but add hybrid join, pre-provisioning, self-deploying, existing-devices modes, user ESP, and up to 100 apps.
flashcards.detail: Pick device preparation for faster, simpler cloud-native Entra join deployments. Pick classic profiles when the scenario needs hybrid join, a technician pre-provisioning step, a self-deploying kiosk, or more apps than the device preparation limits.

flashcards.front: Upgrading Windows 10 devices to Windows 11 with Intune
flashcards.back: Use a feature update deployment profile that targets a Windows 11 version. Devices that meet the requirements upgrade; ineligible devices stay on Windows 10 unless the option to install the latest Windows 10 feature update on devices that cannot run Windows 11 is selected. Endpoint analytics readiness reports show which devices meet hardware requirements.
flashcards.detail: The checkbox cannot be changed on an existing policy, because changing it ends one deployment and starts two. Create a new policy instead. Submitting the policy accepts the Windows 11 license terms on behalf of users, so no user prompt appears.

flashcards.front: Windows settings backup and restore (formerly Windows Backup for Organizations)
flashcards.back: A Windows 11 feature that backs up user settings and the list of Microsoft Store apps for users signed in with Microsoft Entra ID, then restores them on a new device during OOBE or at first sign-in. It is off by default until backup and restore policies are configured, and backups run about every eight days.
flashcards.detail: Configure backup with a settings catalog policy. Restore can be turned on tenant-wide for enrollment (Devices > Enrollment > Windows Backup and Restore) or with a settings catalog policy after enrollment. During Autopilot, the profile must be user-driven, not self-deploying.

flashcards.back: A Cloud PC is built from a gallery image or a custom image. Gallery images are replicated to all regions, updated monthly, and come with or without Microsoft 365 Apps preinstalled. Custom images must be generation 2, generalized, single-session, never joined to a domain, Entra ID, or Intune, and stored as a managed image or in an Azure Compute Gallery.
flashcards.detail: Images cannot contain FSLogix components or a recovery partition, and multi-session images are not supported. The image is chosen in the provisioning policy.

flashcards.back: A provisioning policy can place Cloud PCs on a Microsoft-hosted network or on your own virtual network through an Azure network connection (ANC). The ANC is needed for access to on-premises resources and for hybrid Microsoft Entra join, and it needs health checks to pass.
flashcards.detail: Use the Microsoft-hosted network when Cloud PCs only need internet and cloud apps, since there is nothing to build or maintain. Use an ANC when the Cloud PCs must reach private resources, which brings the extra roles and network requirements.

flashcards.back: Specialty device management covers devices such as Microsoft Teams Rooms, HoloLens 2, and other AR/VR or smart-screen devices, and needs Intune Plan 2 or the advanced capabilities. Zebra Android devices are tuned with OEMConfig profiles: Zebra OEMConfig Powered by MX for newer Android versions and the legacy OEMConfig app for older ones.
flashcards.detail: On Zebra devices, do not configure the same top-level group in several OEMConfig profiles, since that creates conflicts, and keep settings in as few profiles as possible because multiple profiles take longer to deploy.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Tunnel for Mobile Application Management (Tunnel for MAM)
flashcards.back: Tunnel for MAM extends the Microsoft Tunnel VPN gateway to Android and iOS/iPadOS devices that are not enrolled in Intune, so BYOD users reach on-premises resources through managed apps. It requires an existing Tunnel gateway and Intune Plan 2 or an additional license.
flashcards.detail: On Android, VPN comes through the Defender app (with Company Portal installed) and can be per-app or device-wide. On iOS/iPadOS it uses the Tunnel for MAM SDK in the app and is per-app only. Edge can enforce strict tunnel mode, which blocks traffic when the VPN is down.

flashcards.front: Update Microsoft Defender security intelligence remote action
flashcards.back: The Update Windows Defender security intelligence action tells a Windows device to refresh its Microsoft Defender Antivirus definitions immediately, and quick scan and full scan actions run a scan on demand, all from the device page in Intune.
flashcards.detail: It is the quick response when a new threat is announced, or when a device missed scheduled updates. It does not change antivirus policy, only triggers an immediate update.

flashcards.back: Intune can run supported remote actions on up to 100 devices at once from Devices > All devices > Bulk device actions, for example wipe, retire, and delete. Bulk requests count toward the tenant's daily limit for each action, together with individual and Graph API requests.
flashcards.detail: It suits end-of-term resets or fleet-wide restarts. For larger sets, split the work into several batches or use the Microsoft Graph API, remembering that the daily limit is shared across all submission methods.

flashcards.back: The BitLocker key rotation action generates a new recovery key for the OS drive of an encrypted Windows device, so a key that was read aloud or exposed becomes useless. Run it from the device page under Secure; roles such as Help Desk Operator and Endpoint Security Manager include the permission.
flashcards.detail: The old key stops working once the new one is escrowed. Check that the new key has been escrowed to Microsoft Entra ID before relying on it.

flashcards.back: The action forces a new password for the managed local administrator account outside the Windows LAPS schedule, for example after a suspected compromise or a support session. It works on corporate-owned Windows devices that are Entra joined or hybrid joined and already back up their LAPS password to Microsoft Entra ID.
flashcards.detail: It also works for macOS devices enrolled with Automated Device Enrollment whose local admin account is defined in the ADE profile. A custom role needs the Rotate Local Admin Password remote task permission.

flashcards.back: Enrollment time grouping lets an Intune enrollment policy place a device in a specific Microsoft Entra security group during enrollment, so group-targeted policies and apps reach the device earlier in setup. It is generally available for Apple automated device enrollment on iOS/iPadOS and macOS.
flashcards.detail: Normally a device only lands in a dynamic group after enrollment finishes, so required apps and policies arrive late. Targeting a static group at enrollment time avoids that delay. Assignment filters are the complementary tool for narrowing a profile to the right devices.

flashcards.front: Software update policies for iOS/iPadOS and macOS
flashcards.back: Apple update policies are created in the settings catalog with Declarative Device Management. A Latest version policy installs the newest eligible OS after a delay in days at an install time, while a Targeted version policy requires a specific OS version by a deadline and can show a details URL. The older MDM-based update policies are deprecated.
flashcards.detail: Devices enforce the declaration on their own, so the device does not wait for an MDM command. Use targeted version when an app must be validated first, and latest version for fast patching with minimal IT effort.

flashcards.back: FOTA lets Intune manage firmware updates for corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices (fully managed, dedicated, and corporate-owned work profile). Samsung devices use Knox E-FOTA and Zebra devices use LifeGuard OTA; where FOTA is unavailable, a device restrictions profile controls system updates and can set a freeze period.
flashcards.detail: FOTA is an Intune Plan 2 capability. A freeze period blocks over-the-air updates for a defined window, such as a holiday sales peak, but not every manufacturer supports over-the-air control.

flashcards.back: Deployment plans (public preview) are reusable templates that define rings of group assignments with deferral days and hours between them. A deployment applies a plan to a specific app or policy so it reaches devices in controlled stages, found under Devices > Manage devices > Deployments.
flashcards.detail: A ring that uses the All users or All devices virtual group is always the last ring. Plans hold no payload; the payload is chosen when you create the deployment.

flashcards.back: An EDR policy in Intune endpoint security deploys the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint onboarding configuration and EDR settings, such as sample sharing and telemetry reporting frequency, to devices through a policy assigned to device groups. The Defender for Endpoint connector must be turned on first.
flashcards.detail: Onboarding makes the device visible in the Microsoft Defender portal, where analysts investigate alerts, triage incidents, and can isolate or scan a device. Intune then uses the device risk level in compliance policies and Conditional Access.

flashcards.back: Intune security baselines are Microsoft-recommended setting groups for Windows, Edge, Microsoft 365 Apps, and Windows 365. Each Windows release gets a new baseline version, such as Windows 11 version 26H2, and existing profiles never update automatically, so an admin must create a new profile or update one to the new version.
flashcards.detail: Review the changed settings before moving to a newer version, since defaults can change and some settings are retired. Use a pilot group first, then widen the assignment.

flashcards.front: Defender for Endpoint integration with Intune compliance
flashcards.back: Once Intune is connected to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, a compliance policy can require a machine risk score at or below a chosen level. A device above that level is marked noncompliant, and Conditional Access can then block it from company resources until it is remediated.
flashcards.detail: The risk level comes from Defender for Endpoint's detection of active threats, not from Intune settings. Pair it with actions for noncompliance so the user is notified or the device is retired after a grace period.

flashcards.back: Quiet time policies, created under Apps > Quiet Time, automatically mute Outlook email and Teams notifications on iOS/iPadOS and Android during set periods. The three types are date range, days of the week (all day or certain hours), and non-working time, which relies on the Working Time API for Teams.
flashcards.detail: Policies assign to user groups and edits can take about 24 hours to reach users. Quiet time is not supported in sovereign clouds such as GCC High, DoD, and 21Vianet.

flashcards.back: The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center manages Microsoft 365 Apps installed on Windows and Mac devices: servicing profiles for update channels and timing, inventory and health of installed apps, and policy management for Microsoft 365 Apps settings through cloud policy.
flashcards.detail: Use Intune to deploy the apps, and the Apps admin center to control their servicing and policies. The Office Deployment Tool with a configuration file is the alternative to Intune's built-in Microsoft 365 Apps app type for custom installs.

flashcards.front: Deploying Microsoft 365 Apps during Windows Autopilot
flashcards.back: Assign the Microsoft 365 Apps app type (or an ODT-based Win32 app) as a required install to the device group used by the Autopilot profile, and list it in the Enrollment Status Page required apps so the device is not released until Office is installed.
flashcards.detail: The ESP can only wait for apps that actually target the device or signed-in user during setup. A recent change also makes the Intune Management Extension check for app assignments right after ESP completes, reducing the wait for remaining Win32 apps.

flashcards.front: Monitoring app deployments and troubleshooting installs
flashcards.back: Use Apps > Monitor and the app's Device install status and User install status for failures, then use the Troubleshooting + support page and the Collect diagnostics action for a device. On Windows, Win32 app installs are traced in the Intune Management Extension logs.
flashcards.detail: A failure code with the install command tells you whether packaging, detection rules, requirements, or dependencies are at fault. A detection rule that does not match is a frequent cause of an app that installs but is reported as not installed.

flashcards.back: Intune now uses push notifications when an admin changes a Win32 app, so managed devices check in sooner instead of waiting for the next polling interval. The Intune Management Extension also checks for new app assignments immediately after the Enrollment Status Page completes.
flashcards.detail: This shortens the gap between assigning an app and seeing it install. It does not remove the need for correct detection rules, requirements, and dependencies.

flashcards.back: A Security Copilot agent in Intune that evaluates Multi Admin Approval requests and recommends whether to approve them, based on risk. Its suggestions can appear inline in the Multi Admin Approval experience for PowerShell scripts.
flashcards.detail: The agent recommends; an approver still decides. This keeps the two-person approval control intact while reducing time spent reviewing each request.

flashcards.back: A Security Copilot agent that uses Microsoft Defender vulnerability data to monitor weaknesses on managed devices and prioritize remediation with AI-driven risk assessments. It now uses Microsoft Entra agentic identity instead of a human user identity.
flashcards.detail: After setup you delegate the required permissions to the agentic identity in the Microsoft Entra and Defender admin centers and run a readiness check. Remediation recommendations still go through admin review.

flashcards.front: Device Offboarding Agent and Policy Configuration Agent
flashcards.back: The Device Offboarding Agent identifies stale or misaligned devices and gives insights before they are offboarded. The Policy Configuration Agent converts plain-language documents and common industry baselines into recommended Intune settings and policies.
flashcards.detail: Both produce recommendations that an admin reviews. They sit alongside Copilot in Intune, which answers questions and troubleshoots, and the standalone Security Copilot portal, which has a security operations focus.

flashcards.back: Copilot in Intune is embedded in the admin center for natural-language data exploration, policy and setting guidance, device troubleshooting, EPM request analysis, and Windows 365 insights. It needs Security Copilot capacity and the Intune plug-in enabled, and it respects Intune RBAC and scope tags.
flashcards.detail: Intune Administrator inherits Security Copilot owner access and other Intune roles inherit contributor access by default, so admins need no extra role assignments. Check the status under Tenant administration > Copilot.

flashcards.back: The anomalies report finds application hangs, crashes, and stop error restarts that appear after changes, groups affected devices into device correlation groups by shared attributes (app version, driver, OS version, model), and flags at-risk devices so admins can fix issues before users report them.
flashcards.detail: Use the device timeline to see events around the anomaly. Detection uses statistical models such as threshold, paired t-test, and Z-score methods, and the thresholds are predetermined, not customizable.

flashcards.back: Advanced Analytics extends endpoint analytics with resource performance (CPU and RAM by device and model), battery health, anomalies, device timeline, device query, multi-device query, and device scopes that use scope tags to filter reports for a subset of devices.
flashcards.detail: It requires a license beyond Intune Plan 1 or Plan 2 (included in Microsoft 365 E3) and supports Intune-managed or co-managed, Entra joined or hybrid joined Windows devices.

flashcards.front: Endpoint analytics scores, baselines, and insights
flashcards.back: Endpoint analytics scores range from 0 to 100 (lower means more room to improve) and a score needs at least five reporting devices. Charts compare you with a built-in All organizations median baseline, and you can create your own baseline to track progress. Insights and recommendations list actions ranked by points gained.
flashcards.detail: Use device and model scores to find problem devices and plan hardware refresh. Startup performance covers boot and sign-in time, and application reliability covers crashes and hangs per app.

flashcards.front: Tenant status and Intune service health
flashcards.back: Tenant administration > Tenant status shows tenant details and service release, connector status (unhealthy when a certificate has expired or the last sync was three or more days ago), service health incidents, issues requiring action, and the Intune message center.
flashcards.detail: Reading service health and message center content needs a role such as Service support administrator or Message Center reader. Review them regularly to build an operational baseline and to spot upcoming changes before they affect devices.

flashcards.front: Intune report export and Graph report APIs
flashcards.back: Reports in the admin center can be filtered, customized, and exported, and larger datasets can be exported with Microsoft Graph export APIs or sent to Log Analytics and Azure Monitor workbooks through diagnostic settings for dashboards and long-term retention.
flashcards.detail: Use built-in reports for current status, Graph export for scheduled automation, and diagnostic settings for retention beyond what the admin center keeps.

questions.question: Contoso is shipping 200 TPM 2.0-equipped shared-floor tablets to a depot. Staff will only unbox and power them on. Nobody signs in during setup, and each tablet must end up joined to Microsoft Entra ID with no primary user. Which Autopilot approach fits?
options: A user-driven profile with Microsoft Entra join, assigned to the depot staff's user group
An Autopilot device preparation policy assigned to the depot staff's user group
A pre-provisioned deployment that uses a user-driven profile, run by the depot staff
A self-deploying profile, assigned to the registered devices through a device group
questions.explanation: A self-deploying profile authenticates the device with its TPM 2.0 attestation, needs no user credentials, and leaves the device with no primary user, so it fits a power-on-only setup. A user-driven profile, with or without pre-provisioning, still ends with a person signing in with their own credentials, which also makes them the primary user. Device preparation policies target users and are likewise user-driven, so someone would still have to sign in.

questions.question: New hires will set up their own laptops at home over slow broadband. At first sign-in, Autopilot spends over an hour on the Enrollment Status Page installing 12 required device apps. The laptops pass through a reseller first and support TPM 2.0 attestation. IT wants the end user's wait cut without changing which apps are required. What should IT do?
options: Switch the deployment profile to self-deploying so provisioning runs unattended without the end user present at the device
Raise the Enrollment Status Page timeout so the installs have longer to finish on the home connection
Use pre-provisioning (white glove) so the device-targeted apps and policies are installed before the laptops ship
Change the 12 apps from Required to Available so users install them later from the Company Portal
questions.explanation: Pre-provisioning moves the device phase, including device-targeted apps and policies, into a technician phase that the reseller completes before shipping, so the new hire only sits through the short user phase. A self-deploying profile removes the user sign-in but would still run every install over the hire's slow connection, and a user-affiliated shipment does not suit it. A longer timeout only prevents a timeout failure, it does not shorten the wait, and making the apps Available changes the requirement the scenario says to keep.

questions.question: A hybrid Microsoft Entra joined fleet is co-managed, with every workload slider still set to Configuration Manager. The company now wants these devices managed by Windows Autopatch. Which change is required before the devices qualify?
options: Uninstall the Configuration Manager client from the devices so that Intune becomes the management authority
Move the Windows Update policies, Device configuration, and Office Click-to-Run apps workloads to Intune or Pilot Intune
Move the Compliance policies workload to Intune, because compliance status is what Autopatch evaluates first
Convert the devices from hybrid Microsoft Entra joined to Microsoft Entra joined and remove their AD computer accounts
questions.explanation: For co-managed devices, Autopatch needs Intune to be authoritative for the workloads that control updates, device configuration, and Microsoft 365 Apps, so those three sliders must be at Pilot Intune or Intune. Compliance policies is a different workload that Autopatch does not depend on. Removing the Configuration Manager client is unnecessary because co-managed devices are supported, and hybrid Entra join is already an eligible join state.

questions.question: A 24/7 operations center complains that monthly patching forces restarts. An admin enables Hotpatch for its eligible Windows devices and tells the team there will be no more restarts. Which statement sets accurate expectations?
options: Devices stay on one baseline and skip cumulative updates until the next feature update arrives
Monthly restarts still happen, but they are held back until the user next signs out of the device
Most monthly security fixes apply in memory without a restart, but periodic baseline updates still restart the device
Restarts are removed for security, driver, and feature updates that arrive through the same update ring and schedule
questions.explanation: Hotpatch applies a subset of security fixes to the running OS in memory, which removes the restart in most months, but not every fix can be applied that way, so devices periodically land on a baseline cumulative update that does restart. Hotpatch does not cover driver or feature updates. It does not merely postpone the restart, and it does not let a device skip cumulative updates altogether.

questions.question: A distribution center has 90 employees on three non-overlapping 8-hour shifts, about 30 per shift. Each worker should get a Windows 365 Cloud PC at the start of their shift, and the company wants to buy the fewest licenses that still work. Which licensing should it buy?
options: Windows 365 Enterprise licenses for all 90 named employees, one per person
Windows 365 Frontline (now Windows 365 Flex) licenses sized for the 30 workers connected at any one time
Windows 365 Enterprise licenses for 30 users, reassigned between shifts as workers rotate
Windows 365 Frontline (now Windows 365 Flex) licenses for all 90 named employees, one per person
questions.explanation: Frontline (renamed Windows 365 Flex in 2026, with licensing unchanged) is licensed by the number of Cloud PCs in use at the same time, not by named user, so 30 Frontline licenses can serve shift workers who never overlap. Enterprise is one license per named user, so buying it for 90 people is the most expensive route. Frontline licenses for all 90 people ignore the concurrency model and waste the saving, and reassigning Enterprise licenses between shifts would repeatedly deprovision the Cloud PCs instead of giving each worker a persistent one.

questions.question: Windows 11 devices sit in an update ring with a 0-day feature update deferral. IT wants them to stay on version 24H2 even after 25H2 is released, while still receiving monthly security updates on the ring's schedule. What should IT assign?
options: A change to the existing ring that raises its feature update deferral to the 365-day maximum
An expedited quality update policy that targets the 24H2 release for these devices
A pause on the update ring until the 25H2 release has been validated in the pilot group
A feature update deployment profile that targets 24H2, keeping the ring for quality updates
questions.explanation: A feature update deployment profile pins the group to a target version, so the devices stay on 24H2 until the profile is changed or removed, while the ring keeps governing monthly quality updates. A deferral only delays the upgrade, so devices move to 25H2 once the 365 days elapse. A pause is temporary and ends automatically after a limited period, and an expedited policy accelerates quality updates and has no say over the feature version.

questions.question: A co-managed, hybrid-joined fleet is run by Configuration Manager. IT wants Intune to take over only Windows Update policies, first for 20 pilot devices and later for everyone, without touching other workloads. What should IT configure?
options: Enable tenant attach and run the update installation action from the cloud console on the 20 devices
Move every workload slider to Pilot Intune and rely on the pilot collection to limit which workloads apply
Set the Windows Update policies slider to Pilot Intune and assign a pilot collection holding those 20 devices
Set the Windows Update policies slider to Intune and exclude the other devices with an assignment filter
questions.explanation: Each workload slider has a Pilot Intune position that applies only to the devices in that workload's pilot collection, so one workload can be staged on 20 devices and later moved to Intune for everyone. Setting the slider to Intune moves the whole fleet at once, and assignment filters live in Intune rather than in the Configuration Manager slider. Moving every workload to Pilot Intune touches workloads the scenario says to leave alone, and tenant attach runs one-off actions without changing which tool is authoritative.

questions.question: The Group Policy setting for automatic MDM enrollment is applied to hybrid Microsoft Entra joined Windows 11 PCs, yet none of them appear in Intune. The users are licensed. What should the admin check first?
options: That the Intune Connector for Active Directory is installed on a domain-joined server
That the MDM user scope in Microsoft Entra ID includes the users who sign in to those PCs
That an Autopilot deployment profile is assigned to the PCs, since it triggers enrollment
That a compliance policy is assigned to the PCs so that Intune can recognize them
questions.explanation: Automatic enrollment through Group Policy still depends on the MDM user scope in Microsoft Entra ID, so users outside that scope never enroll even though the policy applies and the PCs are hybrid joined. Autopilot is a provisioning path for new or reset devices, not a prerequisite for GPO enrollment. A compliance policy is assigned after a device exists in Intune, and the Intune Connector for Active Directory only supports Autopilot hybrid join, where it creates the computer object.

questions.question: A specific laptop model is not being offered the latest Windows feature update through its update ring, even though every configured deferral period has already elapsed. What is the most likely explanation?
options: The laptops are failing their compliance policy, and noncompliant devices are excluded from feature update rollout
A driver update policy set to manual approval is also holding back feature updates for the same devices
A safeguard hold, applied by Microsoft after detecting a known compatibility issue with that hardware, is blocking the update
The ring's feature deferral counts from each device's enrollment date, not the release date, so it has not elapsed yet
questions.explanation: A safeguard hold is applied automatically by Microsoft when it detects a known compatibility problem for a device or hardware and driver combination, and it blocks that feature update until Microsoft lifts it or an admin deliberately opts out of safeguard holds. Deferral days count from the release date, so the stem's elapsed deferrals rule out a timing cause. Compliance status does not gate feature update offers, and a driver update policy governs drivers only.
questions.whyTested: This is one of the exam's favorite 'don't blame your own configuration' traps: admin misconfiguration is the intuitive first guess, and the question tests whether you recognize a safeguard hold as something Microsoft deliberately applies, rather than assuming something must be wrong with the ring or a neighbouring policy.

questions.question: New Windows laptops sign in with work accounts and join Microsoft Entra ID successfully, but none ever appear in Intune. All users are licensed, and no enrollment restriction blocks Windows. Which setting should the admin check first?
options: The MAM user scope for Microsoft Intune under Microsoft Entra Mobility (MDM and MAM)
The Entra device setting that limits how many devices each user can join
The tenant-wide compliance setting for devices with no compliance policy assigned
The MDM user scope for Microsoft Intune under Microsoft Entra Mobility (MDM and MAM)
questions.explanation: The MDM user scope decides whose devices are enrolled in Intune automatically when they join Microsoft Entra ID. If it is set to None, or to a group that excludes these users, the join succeeds but no enrollment happens. The MAM user scope only affects app protection on unenrolled devices. A per-user device limit in Entra would block the join itself, which the stem says succeeds, and the no-policy compliance setting changes how compliance is reported, not whether a device enrolls.

questions.question: Contoso's default enrollment restriction blocks personally owned Windows devices. A higher-priority restriction that allows personal Windows devices is assigned to a group containing the IT team's laptops, yet IT staff still cannot enroll personal devices. What should be changed?
options: Add a device limit restriction for the group that holds the IT team's laptops
Replace the platform restriction with a compliance policy that blocks personal Windows devices
Assign the allowing restriction to a user group that contains the IT staff
Move the allowing restriction below the default restriction in priority
questions.explanation: Enrollment restrictions are evaluated for the user who is enrolling, so they must be assigned to user groups. Assigning one to a group of devices means it never applies at enrollment. Priority is already higher than the default, and lowering it would reverse the intent. A device limit caps the number of devices rather than the ownership type, and a compliance policy only acts after enrollment, so it cannot block enrollment.

questions.question: Contoso is retiring on-premises GPOs and moving Windows 11 devices to Intune. The admin wants to learn which GPO settings have MDM equivalents and generate Intune policy from the ones that do, with minimal manual work. What should the admin use?
options: A security baseline, which imports the existing GPOs and mirrors their settings across the Windows 11 devices
Group Policy analytics, migrating supported settings from an imported GPO into a settings catalog profile
The Administrative templates profile type, with the admin recreating each GPO setting manually in the profile
A custom OMA-URI profile that the admin builds by hand from each setting's ADMX file, one setting at a time
questions.explanation: Group Policy analytics analyzes an exported GPO, reports which settings have MDM support, and can migrate the supported ones into a settings catalog profile, which removes most of the manual work. A hand-built OMA-URI profile and recreating settings in Administrative templates both do that work by hand, and a security baseline is a Microsoft-defined set of recommended values that does not read your existing GPOs.

questions.question: Domain-joined Windows 11 desktops must become hybrid Microsoft Entra joined so Conditional Access can evaluate them. The admin runs the Microsoft Entra Connect wizard and selects the hybrid join option. What does this configure so the desktops can find the tenant and register themselves?
options: A service connection point in AD that points the desktops to the tenant
The Intune Connector for Active Directory on a domain-joined server in the forest
A Group Policy setting for automatic MDM enrollment into Intune for the desktops
An Autopilot hybrid join profile assigned to the desktops' device group
questions.explanation: For hybrid join, Microsoft Entra Connect publishes a service connection point in Active Directory that tells domain-joined Windows devices which tenant to register with, and they then register themselves. Automatic MDM enrollment through Group Policy is a later step that depends on hybrid join already working. The Intune Connector for Active Directory supports Autopilot by creating computer objects for new devices, and an Autopilot profile applies to new or reset devices rather than desktops that are already domain-joined.

questions.question: A user holds Microsoft 365 E3 and has just been assigned a Windows 365 Enterprise license. The user does not belong to any group that Cloud PC provisioning targets. What is the result?
options: A Cloud PC is created automatically with default settings, as happens for Windows 365 Business licenses
No Cloud PC is created until the user belongs to a group assigned to a provisioning policy
A Cloud PC is created once an admin also assigns the user a separate Intune device license
A Cloud PC is created the first time the user signs in to the Windows 365 portal
questions.explanation: In Windows 365 Enterprise, a Cloud PC is created only when the user both holds a Windows 365 license and falls inside a group assigned to a provisioning policy. Automatic provisioning on license assignment describes Windows 365 Business, not Enterprise. Microsoft 365 E3 already includes Intune, so no extra Intune license is needed, and a portal sign-in does not trigger creation.

questions.question: Berlin helpdesk admins must see only Berlin's policies and apps, and may run remote actions only on devices of Berlin users. Which settings on their Intune role assignment satisfy both requirements?
options: Scope (Groups) containing Berlin users and devices, which also hides other regions' policies and apps from the admin
An assignment filter on each Berlin policy, which restricts what administrators can see in the admin center
A Berlin scope tag on the role assignment, which also limits which devices the admin can target with remote actions
A Berlin scope tag for object visibility, plus Scope (Groups) containing Berlin users and devices for what they can target
questions.explanation: A role assignment has two separate limits: scope tags control which Intune objects an admin can see, and Scope (Groups) controls which users and devices the admin can act on. The scenario needs both, so using only one leaves either the visibility or the targeting wide open. Assignment filters narrow which devices receive an assigned item and have no effect on what an administrator can see.

questions.question: In the Intune admin center the Intune Connector for Active Directory shows as active, yet user-driven hybrid Autopilot devices fail at domain join and no device accounts appear in AD. What should the admin verify first?
options: That a compliance policy is assigned to the devices before they begin their provisioning run
That each device's hardware hash was registered with the correct group tag before it shipped
That the Enrollment Status Page timeout is long enough for the domain join step to complete
That the connector's account can create computer objects in the Domain Join profile's OU
questions.explanation: The connector creates the computer object in the OU named in the Domain Join profile, so it needs permission to create computer objects there. An active status does not prove that permission exists. A short ESP timeout would fail later in provisioning, a wrong group tag would stop the profile from assigning before the domain-join stage, and compliance policies are not evaluated before provisioning.

questions.question: A configuration profile is assigned to All devices. IT wants it to skip Windows 10 devices, without creating or maintaining any new groups and while keeping the All devices assignment. What should be added?
options: An excluded Entra user group that contains the owners of the Windows 10 devices
A dynamic device group for Windows 11 that replaces the All devices assignment
An assignment filter in include mode that matches the Windows 11 OS version range
A scope tag that is applied to the Windows 11 devices
questions.explanation: An assignment filter evaluates device properties such as OS version on top of the existing assignment, so All devices stays in place and no group is needed. Intune does not evaluate a user-group exclusion against a device-targeted assignment, a scope tag only limits which admins can see an object, and a dynamic device group would work but breaks the stated constraints by adding a group and replacing the assignment.

questions.question: Conditional Access requires a compliant device for Exchange Online. Auditors found that a newly enrolled laptop, which has not yet received any compliance policy, can still open mail. Which tenant-wide Intune setting should change?
options: Set the Mark device noncompliant action to 0 days in every compliance policy
Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as Not compliant
Shorten the compliance status validity period to one day
Turn on enhanced jailbreak detection for mobile devices
questions.explanation: By default, a device with no compliance policy assigned is reported as compliant, which is why the new laptop passes the Conditional Access check. Flipping that setting to Not compliant closes the gap. The validity period only affects devices that stop checking in, enhanced jailbreak detection is a mobile setting, and a 0-day noncompliance action lives inside individual policies, which the new laptop has not received.

questions.question: A Conditional Access policy requires a compliant device for Exchange Online. A user signs in from a compliant corporate laptop and from their own noncompliant, Intune-enrolled phone. What happens?
options: The laptop is blocked as well, because requiring a compliant device also implies a hybrid Microsoft Entra joined device
Both are granted, because the policy is satisfied once one of the user's devices is compliant
The laptop gets access and the phone is blocked, because compliance is evaluated for the specific device used at each sign-in
Both are blocked until the phone is remediated, because compliance follows the user across their registered devices
questions.explanation: The require device to be marked as compliant grant control is device-bound, so it checks the device used for that particular sign-in. The compliant laptop passes and the noncompliant phone is blocked. Compliance is not pooled across a user's devices in either direction, and hybrid join is a different grant control that this policy does not include.
questions.whyTested: MD-102 repeatedly tests whether you track a Conditional Access grant control at the device level or the user level, because that single detail flips the answer between 'blocked everywhere' and 'blocked only on this one device', a distinction real admins get wrong when troubleshooting an access ticket.

questions.question: Security wants Windows devices that Microsoft Defender for Endpoint rates as high risk to lose Conditional Access-gated access automatically. The devices are Intune-enrolled but not yet onboarded to Defender for Endpoint. Which step should the admin do first?
options: Deploy an attack surface reduction policy in audit mode to the Windows devices
Turn on the Intune connection to Defender for Endpoint in the admin center
Add a machine risk score requirement to the Windows compliance policy for the laptops
Create the Conditional Access policy that requires a compliant device for Exchange Online
questions.explanation: The connection between Intune and Defender for Endpoint comes first because it lets Intune deploy the onboarding configuration and receive each device's risk signal. The machine risk rule in the compliance policy and the Conditional Access policy that consumes the result build on top of that connection and onboarding. An attack surface reduction policy in audit mode neither onboards devices nor feeds compliance.

questions.question: A security baseline profile was assigned to a device group a year ago. Microsoft has since released a newer baseline version, but devices still enforce the old settings. IT wants the new defaults without recreating the profile or its assignments. What should IT do?
options: Create a new profile from the newer baseline, since existing instances stay locked to their original version
Wait for the next device check-in, when assigned baselines update to the latest version automatically
Remove and re-add the devices to the assigned group so that the baseline is re-evaluated
Move the existing profile instance to the newer baseline version, then review its settings
questions.explanation: Baselines are versioned, and an existing profile instance picks up a newer version only when an admin moves it to that version, which keeps its assignments in place. Nothing updates automatically at check-in, a new profile is not required because instances can be moved, and changing group membership has no effect on which baseline version the profile uses.

questions.question: A help desk technician reads a BitLocker recovery key aloud to a user during a call. Security now wants each key to become invalid once it has been used for recovery, with no technician action afterward. Keys are already escrowed to Microsoft Entra ID. What should be added?
options: A Rotate BitLocker keys remote action, run by a technician after each recovery call
Client-driven recovery password rotation, enabled in the disk encryption policy
A compliance policy that requires BitLocker and regenerates the key at its next evaluation
A Wipe action sent to each device after its recovery key has been used
questions.explanation: Client-driven recovery password rotation makes the device generate a new recovery password and escrow it after the old one is used, which needs no one to act afterward. The Rotate BitLocker keys remote action also works but depends on a technician remembering to run it. Wiping the device destroys data to solve a key problem, and compliance policies check for BitLocker without regenerating keys.

questions.question: Developers must run one IT-approved installer that needs administrator rights every time it runs. Security wants administrator rights limited to that installer, a typed reason from the developer each time, and no developer added to the local Administrators group. What should be configured?
options: An Endpoint Privilege Management elevation rule for that file, with user-confirmed elevation and required justification
A Win32 app deployment that reinstalls the tool under the SYSTEM account whenever the developers need to run it
A local user group membership policy that adds the developers to the Administrators group on their laptops
A Windows LAPS policy that lets the developers retrieve the rotated local administrator password for each device
questions.explanation: An Endpoint Privilege Management rule elevates only the specific approved file, and the user-confirmed type can require a business justification, with no change to group membership. LAPS would hand developers a full administrator credential, adding them to the Administrators group is exactly what security forbids, and reinstalling the tool does not help when the program needs elevation each time it runs.

questions.question: A Win32 app must install on shared Autopilot kiosks during provisioning, before any user ever signs in, and the Enrollment Status Page must wait for it. How should the app be assigned?
options: Required, assigned to a user group that contains the staff who will use the kiosks
Required, assigned to a device group that contains the kiosks
Available for enrolled devices, assigned to the kiosk device group
Required, assigned to All users with a filter that matches the kiosks
questions.explanation: A required assignment to a device group installs during the device phase with no user present, and the Enrollment Status Page can track it. A user-targeted assignment waits for someone to sign in, which never happens on an unattended kiosk, and an Available assignment only appears in the Company Portal for a person to start, so the ESP cannot wait on it.

questions.question: Employees check corporate email in Outlook on their own unenrolled phones. The company wants a required PIN and a block on copying corporate data into unmanaged apps, without enrolling any of these phones in MDM. What should be deployed?
options: A device compliance policy for the personal phones, since compliance policies can enforce PIN and copy-paste restrictions the same way
A device configuration profile that requires MDM enrollment first, since PIN and copy-paste controls are profile settings, not app settings
A security baseline scoped to the Outlook app, since baselines can target individual applications instead of only devices
An app protection (MAM) policy targeting Outlook, which applies its controls at the app level whatever the device's management state
questions.explanation: An app protection policy enforces a PIN and copy-paste limits inside the app and works on devices that are not MDM-enrolled, which is exactly this BYOD requirement. Compliance policies and configuration profiles need an enrolled device to apply, and security baselines target devices, not individual apps.
questions.whyTested: Exams stack four plausible-sounding controls, compliance policy, configuration profile, security baseline, and app protection policy, that all sound capable of enforcing a PIN, to test whether you know which single one operates below the MDM-enrollment line, since that detail makes or breaks a BYOD deployment.

questions.question: Employees use Outlook on personal iPhones that are not enrolled in Intune. IT wants each user's mailbox settings pre-filled so nobody types server details. What should IT create?
options: An app configuration policy that targets managed devices and supplies the Outlook settings
A device configuration email profile assigned to the users
An app protection policy whose data transfer settings contain the mailbox details
An app configuration policy that targets managed apps and supplies the Outlook settings
questions.explanation: An app configuration policy that targets managed apps delivers settings to the app through the app protection channel, so it works without device enrollment. The managed devices variant relies on MDM and needs an enrolled device, an app protection policy enforces controls such as data transfer rules rather than delivering account settings, and an email profile is an MDM payload that also needs enrollment.

questions.question: Contoso allows corporate mail on unenrolled personal phones. An audit found that an approved mail app connected from a phone where Intune had applied no data controls to it. Which current Conditional Access grant control closes that gap?
options: Require app protection policy
Require multifactor authentication
Require approved client app (legacy control, retired June 2026)
Require device to be marked as compliant
questions.explanation: Requiring an app protection policy goes beyond checking the app's identity and demands that a compliant policy is actually applied to it. The legacy require approved client app control (retired in June 2026 in favor of require app protection policy) only checked the app against Microsoft's list, which is how the audit gap arose. An unenrolled personal phone can never be marked compliant, so that control would block every user, and multifactor authentication proves who is signing in but says nothing about the app's protection.

questions.question: Contoso needs Wi-Fi authentication certificates on managed laptops. There must be no on-premises CA or NDES server, and each private key must be generated on the device and never leave it. What should be deployed?
options: Imported PFX certificates that a third-party CA generated, delivered to each laptop with its private key
A PKCS certificate profile that uses the Intune Certificate Connector with an on-premises certificate authority
A SCEP certificate profile that requests from Microsoft Cloud PKI, plus a trusted certificate profile for the root CA
A SCEP certificate profile that points at an on-premises NDES server running the certificate connector
questions.explanation: Cloud PKI is a cloud-hosted CA that issues through SCEP, so devices generate their own keys and no on-premises CA or NDES is needed. The PKCS option relies on a connector and on-premises CA and creates the key off the device, a SCEP profile pointed at NDES keeps the on-premises server the company wants to avoid, and imported PFX certificates arrive with a private key that was generated elsewhere.

questions.question: Tier-1 technicians must be limited to viewing a user's screen, while tier-2 technicians may take full control. Both the helper and the user must sign in with Microsoft Entra ID, and sessions must be tied to technician roles rather than a shared code. What should IT use?
options: Remote Help, with role-based access control setting each technician's permission level
A device configuration profile that enables Remote Desktop and lists the technicians
Quick Assist, with technicians giving users a security code to start each session
A Microsoft Defender live response session started from the Defender portal
questions.explanation: Remote Help is the Intune-integrated tool in which both parties sign in with Microsoft Entra ID and role-based access control decides between view only and full control. Quick Assist works with a code and has no role-based permission levels tied to Intune, Remote Desktop gives no per-role view-only mode or user consent flow, and live response is a security investigation shell rather than a screen-sharing support tool.

questions.question: An admin must create 40 near-identical configuration profiles in one tenant, changing only the assigned group and one setting value, and later repeat the work in a second tenant. Which approach removes the most manual effort?
options: Create one profile and duplicate it 40 times in the admin center, editing each copy
Script the creation with the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK against the Intune endpoints
Build the profiles in Intune and feed the Intune Data Warehouse into Power BI for reuse
Deploy a PowerShell script from the Scripts node so it runs on the managed devices
questions.explanation: Intune objects are exposed through Microsoft Graph, so a script using the Graph PowerShell SDK can create all 40 profiles and be re-run against another tenant. A script deployed from the Scripts node runs on managed devices to configure them and cannot create tenant objects. The Data Warehouse is a read-only reporting feed, and duplicating in the admin center is still 40 manual passes that would be repeated for the second tenant.

questions.question: The security team needs Conditional Access to block Windows laptops where a specific registry value is missing. No built-in compliance setting evaluates that value, and the team does not need automatic correction. What should the admin create?
options: A custom OMA-URI configuration profile that reads the registry key on the laptops
A settings catalog profile that sets the registry value on the laptops
A proactive remediation that has a detection script and no remediation script, assigned to the laptops
A custom compliance policy that pairs a PowerShell discovery script with a JSON rules file
questions.explanation: Only a compliance policy feeds the compliance state that Conditional Access reads, and a custom compliance policy lets a script report the registry value and a JSON file define what counts as compliant. A remediation's detection result does not change compliance state, and configuration profiles such as OMA-URI or settings catalog push a value instead of evaluating one.
questions.whyTested: Several real Intune features, remediations, OMA-URI profiles, and settings catalog profiles, sound capable of checking a registry value, but only a custom compliance policy feeds the compliance state that Conditional Access reads. The question tests whether you can separate evaluate-and-report from configure and from detect-and-fix.

questions.question: A background service stops intermittently on 300 Windows laptops, sometimes weeks after deployment. The team wants a check every hour that restarts the service only when it is down, so users never file a ticket. What should they deploy?
options: A proactive remediation with a detection script and a remediation script, scheduled hourly
A custom compliance policy whose discovery script checks the service status on each laptop
A platform PowerShell script that restarts the service, assigned to the laptops
An alert rule that notifies the team by email when the service stops on a laptop
questions.explanation: A proactive remediation runs a detection script on a schedule and, only when it reports a problem, runs the paired remediation script, which matches an hourly check-and-fix. A platform PowerShell script runs once unless it changes, so it would not catch a later failure. A custom compliance policy only reports status, and an alert rule notifies people about a signal without repairing anything.

questions.question: The finance team's Excel add-in hangs and crashes repeatedly. IT wants a score broken down by app and by device model, so it can prioritize which apps to fix first. Which Endpoint analytics report fits?
options: Work from anywhere
Resource performance
Startup performance
Application reliability
questions.explanation: Application reliability scores how often apps crash or hang and breaks the results down by app and by device model, which is what the team needs. Startup performance measures boot and sign-in time, Work from anywhere assesses cloud readiness of identity, management, and provisioning, and Resource performance scores whether device CPU and memory are adequate.

questions.question: A device shows conflicting policy results. The admin wants a plain-language summary of the conflict and suggested next steps inside the Intune admin center, then decides personally whether to change anything. What should the admin use?
options: An alert rule on the profile failure rate
Endpoint analytics Application reliability
The Troubleshooting + support page for that device
A Security Copilot agent integrated with Intune
questions.explanation: Security Copilot in Intune accepts natural-language prompts, summarizes issues such as policy conflicts, and suggests remediation steps for an admin to review before any change is made. Troubleshooting + support shows assignment and deployment status for a device but does not generate a summary or suggestions, Application reliability scores app crashes, and an alert rule only notifies when a threshold is crossed.

questions.question: When a feature update deployment profile targets devices that also receive an update ring, the ring's feature update deferral no longer delays the feature update for those devices.
questions.explanation: This sounds wrong because the deferral is still configured in the ring, but the deployment profile takes precedence over the ring's feature deferral for its devices. The ring continues to govern their quality updates.

questions.question: Contoso is registering devices with Windows Autopatch. Assuming licensing requirements are met, which of these devices is eligible?
options: A Windows 11 PC joined to on-premises AD and managed through the Configuration Manager client
A Windows 11 laptop that is Microsoft Entra joined and enrolled in Intune
A personal Windows 11 laptop that is Microsoft Entra registered, with the user's work account added
An iPad enrolled in Intune through Automated Device Enrollment
questions.explanation: Autopatch manages Windows devices that are Microsoft Entra joined or hybrid joined and already managed by Intune. A device that is merely Entra registered is a personal-device state outside that requirement, a PC managed only by Configuration Manager has neither an Entra join nor Intune management, and Autopatch does not manage iPads.

questions.question: A self-deploying Autopilot profile can hybrid Microsoft Entra join a device, provided the Intune Connector for Active Directory is installed.
questions.explanation: Self-deploying profiles support Microsoft Entra join only. Hybrid join through Autopilot needs a user-driven profile, with the Intune Connector for Active Directory creating the on-premises computer object.

questions.question: A co-managed device keeps its Configuration Manager client installed even after every co-management workload slider has been moved to Intune.
questions.explanation: Workload sliders only change which tool is authoritative for each workload. They do not remove the Configuration Manager client, which stays on the device until it is retired separately.

questions.question: A custom OMA-URI profile is the preferred way to configure a newly released Windows setting, ahead of the settings catalog.
questions.explanation: The settings catalog exposes CSP-backed settings individually and is kept current, so it is the first place to look. A custom OMA-URI profile is a fallback for a setting the catalog or a template does not expose.

questions.question: If a user belongs to groups targeted by several enrollment restrictions of the same type, Intune applies only the highest-priority one rather than combining them.
questions.explanation: Restrictions of the same type are not merged. The user gets the one with the highest priority among those assigned to their groups, and the built-in default restriction applies only when no assigned restriction covers them.

questions.question: Contoso's Cloud PCs must be hybrid Microsoft Entra joined so users can reach on-premises file shares and apply domain policy. Which provisioning policy configuration is required?
options: A Microsoft Entra join policy that Intune enrollment later converts into hybrid join
A hybrid join policy that uses an Azure network connection with domain join details
A Microsoft Entra join policy that uses the Microsoft-hosted network and the default image
A hybrid join policy that uses the Microsoft-hosted network with domain join details
questions.explanation: Hybrid Entra joined Cloud PCs need an Azure network connection that can reach a domain controller and carries the domain join settings. The Microsoft-hosted network supports Microsoft Entra join only, so it cannot be paired with hybrid join, and enrolling a Cloud PC in Intune does not convert its join type.

questions.question: A Conditional Access policy that requires a compliant device for all cloud apps should keep the Microsoft Intune Enrollment cloud app included, so that only already-compliant devices can enroll.
questions.explanation: A device cannot be compliant before it has enrolled, so including the Microsoft Intune Enrollment cloud app creates a catch-22 that blocks new enrollments. It should be excluded from the compliance requirement.

questions.question: By default, a user can view the BitLocker recovery key of their own Microsoft Entra joined device in the My Account portal.
questions.explanation: This sounds risky but is the default: the Entra device setting that restricts users from recovering their own BitLocker keys is off. An admin can turn it on when keys should only be released by the help desk.

questions.question: Which two statements about Endpoint Privilege Management elevation rules are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: A rule can require the user to enter a business justification before elevation proceeds
A rule adds the user to the local Administrators group for the rest of the session
Rules apply to any Microsoft Entra registered device, including personal phones
A rule can target a specific file by its hash or its signing certificate
A rule removes the need for the device to be managed by Intune
questions.explanation: Elevation rules identify an approved file by attributes such as its hash or certificate, and they can require a justification before elevating. A rule elevates only that application and never changes group membership, and it works on Intune-managed Windows devices rather than registered personal phones or unmanaged machines.

questions.question: Contoso allows personal Android phones, and users agree to enroll them. IT wants a separate work container with its own managed apps, Wi-Fi, and VPN settings, and a wipe that removes only work data. Which approach fits?
options: Android Enterprise fully managed enrollment
An app protection policy on unenrolled phones
Android device administrator enrollment
Android Enterprise personal work profile enrollment
questions.explanation: A personal work profile keeps corporate apps and settings, including Wi-Fi and VPN, in an isolated container that IT can wipe on its own, and it relies on MDM enrollment, which the users have agreed to. An app protection policy on unenrolled phones cannot deliver Wi-Fi or VPN settings, fully managed mode is for corporate-owned devices and controls the whole phone, and device administrator is a legacy mode with no separate work container.

questions.question: With a SCEP certificate profile, the private key is generated on the device and never leaves it.
questions.explanation: In SCEP the device creates the key pair and sends only a signing request, so the private key stays on the device. A PKCS profile differs because the key is generated on the server side and delivered to the device.

questions.question: A custom compliance policy needs both a PowerShell discovery script and a JSON file that defines the rules; the script alone is not enough.
questions.explanation: The script reports data from the device, and the JSON file holds the rules and messages that Intune evaluates that data against. Without the JSON file there is nothing to decide compliant or noncompliant.

questions.question: A PowerShell script assigned from the Scripts node in Intune re-runs automatically every hour on the devices it targets.
questions.explanation: A platform script runs once on each targeted device and runs again only if the script changes, or to retry after a failure. Scheduled repeat runs are what a remediation provides.

questions.question: Which two statements about Windows Autopilot deployment profile types are correct? (Choose two.)
options: A self-deploying profile supports Microsoft Entra join but not hybrid Entra join
A user-driven profile can run to completion without any user signing in
A self-deploying profile makes the first person who signs in the device's primary user
Pre-provisioning removes the need for an Enrollment Status Page during the technician phase
A pre-provisioned deployment can use either a user-driven or a self-deploying profile type
questions.explanation: Self-deploying profiles support Microsoft Entra join only, and pre-provisioning can be combined with either user-driven or self-deploying profile types. A user-driven profile cannot finish without a user's credentials, a self-deploying device has no user affiliation and so no primary user, and the Enrollment Status Page is exactly what tracks progress during the technician phase.

questions.question: Which two statements about Windows Autopatch and Hotpatch are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: A hotpatch builds on a current baseline, so a device that fell behind gets a full update with a restart
Hotpatch removes restarts for feature updates delivered through the same deployment ring as security updates
Autopatch manages updates for third-party applications such as Chrome and Adobe Reader as part of its default rings
Autopatch enrollment excludes Microsoft Entra joined devices and accepts hybrid joined ones as the supported state
Autopatch can update Microsoft 365 Apps and Microsoft Edge in addition to Windows quality updates
questions.explanation: Autopatch covers Windows quality updates, drivers and firmware, Microsoft 365 Apps, and Edge, and a hotpatch is a delta on a current baseline, so a device that fell behind receives the full cumulative update with a restart. Autopatch does not manage third-party apps, hotpatching applies to security updates rather than feature updates, and Entra joined devices are eligible alongside hybrid joined ones.

questions.question: Which two statements about Microsoft Entra device states are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: A Microsoft Entra registered device signs users in to Windows with their Entra credentials at the sign-in screen
A Microsoft Entra registered device is typically personal, with a work account added and no organizational control of sign-in
A hybrid Microsoft Entra joined device has an on-premises AD computer account and is also known to Entra ID
Hybrid Entra join is the only device state that can be enrolled in Intune, since joined devices cannot enroll
A Microsoft Entra joined device must also have a computer object in on-premises Active Directory to authenticate
questions.explanation: Hybrid joined devices carry both an AD computer account and an Entra ID device object, and registered devices are typically personal ones where a work account has been added without the organization owning the sign-in. An Entra joined device has no on-premises AD account, Intune can enroll joined, hybrid joined, and registered devices, and signing in to Windows with Entra credentials describes a joined device, not a registered one.

questions.question: Which two statements about compliance policies and Conditional Access are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: Compliance results reach Conditional Access only for corporate-owned devices, not personal ones
An unenrolled phone cannot satisfy the require compliant device control, because Intune holds no state for it
A device that does not check in within the compliance status validity period is treated as noncompliant
A device that passes one assigned compliance policy is compliant even if it fails another assigned policy
A compliance policy blocks sign-in on its own, with no Conditional Access policy required
questions.explanation: Devices that stop reporting are treated as noncompliant once the validity period passes, and a device Intune does not manage has no compliance state to present. A device must meet every assigned policy, compliance by itself only records a status and Conditional Access is what blocks sign-in, and enrolled personal devices do report compliance to Conditional Access.

questions.question: Which two statements about app protection policies and app configuration policies are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: An app protection policy takes effect if Intune deployed the app to the device as a Required install
An app configuration policy can reach managed apps on unenrolled devices when the app supports Intune app configuration
App configuration policies can be targeted to enrolled devices, but not to managed apps
App protection policies are assigned to user groups, so the policy follows the user across devices
An app configuration policy can enforce a PIN and block copy-paste into personal apps on the device
questions.explanation: App configuration can reach managed apps on unenrolled devices, and app protection policies are assigned to users. PIN and copy-paste enforcement belongs to app protection, not app configuration. App protection does not depend on Intune deploying the app, since the app only needs to support the policy, and app configuration is not limited to enrolled devices.

questions.question: Which two statements about Microsoft Cloud PKI and Remote Help are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: Remote Help needs its app on the technician's and the user's devices, each signed in with Microsoft Entra ID
Cloud PKI issues certificates through a SCEP profile that targets the cloud CA, so no NDES server or connector is needed
Remote Help can connect only to devices that are hybrid Microsoft Entra joined to the on-premises domain
Cloud PKI keeps a copy of each issued certificate's private key so it can be downloaded again by the device
Remote Help sessions can start only after the device has been registered with Windows Autopilot in the tenant
questions.explanation: Cloud PKI issues through SCEP, so it removes the NDES server and connector, and Remote Help runs from an app on both ends with Entra sign-in for the technician and user. With SCEP the private key stays on the device and is never stored by the CA, Remote Help also works with Microsoft Entra joined devices, and Autopilot registration is not a prerequisite.

questions.question: Which three statements about remediations and custom compliance policies are accurate? (Choose three.)
options: A custom compliance policy's result feeds the device's compliance state, which Conditional Access can act on
A remediation changes the device's compliance status whenever its detection script finds a problem
A remediation script can be set to run as the signed-in user instead of the default SYSTEM account
A custom compliance discovery script restarts the failed service when it finds it stopped
A remediation's remediation script runs only on devices where its detection script reports an issue
questions.explanation: A custom compliance policy produces a result that Conditional Access can use, a remediation script runs only when the detection script flags a problem, and a remediation can run in the user's context when it needs the user's session. A discovery script only reports data and fixes nothing, and a remediation's detection result does not alter compliance status.

questions.question: New corporate laptops enroll through the Company Portal rather than Autopilot. IT wants users to pick 'Kiosk' or 'Executive' during enrollment, and a dynamic device group to follow that choice. Which device attribute should the group's membership rule use?
options: The Autopilot group tag property
The device ownership property
The device category property
The scope tag assigned to the device
questions.explanation: Device category is the label a user can be prompted to choose at enrollment, and it can be used in dynamic group rules. A group tag exists only on Autopilot registrations, so laptops enrolled through the Company Portal have none. Ownership records corporate versus personal, not purpose, and a scope tag limits which admins can see an object and is not an attribute a dynamic group can filter on.

questions.question: Laptops were registered for Autopilot with the group tag 'Kiosk'. IT needs a dynamic Microsoft Entra device group that contains only those devices, so a deployment profile can be assigned to it. Which membership rule should be used?
options: (device.devicePhysicalIds -any (_ -contains "[ZTDId]"))
(device.deviceCategory -eq "Kiosk")
(device.devicePhysicalIds -any (_ -eq "[PurchaseOrderId]:Kiosk"))
(device.devicePhysicalIds -any (_ -eq "[OrderID]:Kiosk"))
questions.explanation: An Autopilot group tag is stored in the device's physical IDs with the OrderID prefix, so matching [OrderID]:Kiosk selects exactly the tagged devices. The ZTDId rule matches every Autopilot-registered device regardless of tag. PurchaseOrderId matches a different registration attribute, and device category is the label set at enrollment, not something Autopilot registration populates.

questions.question: A zero-day fix was released today. Most update rings defer quality updates seven days. Security needs 40 high-risk laptops patched immediately, even outside active hours, without editing any existing ring. What should the admin create?
options: A change to the existing rings that lowers quality update deferral to zero days for every device
A feature update deployment profile for the 40 laptops that targets the newest Windows version
A driver update policy set to automatic approval for the 40 laptops
An expedited quality update policy for that release, assigned to the 40 laptops
questions.explanation: An expedited quality update policy pushes an already-released fix to a targeted group right away, bypassing the ring's deferral and active hours, and leaves every existing ring untouched. A feature update profile governs the Windows version, not a monthly security fix, and a driver update policy governs drivers. Lowering deferral on the existing rings breaks the no-edit constraint and would also pull the fix forward for every other device.

questions.question: Configuration Manager devices have been uploaded to the Intune admin center with tenant attach. Security now wants Conditional Access to require a compliant device for them, using Intune compliance policies. What must be done?
options: Move the Endpoint Protection workload to Intune, since it evaluates device health
Move the Resource access policies workload to Intune, since it holds the compliance settings
Enable co-management and move the Compliance policies workload to Intune
Nothing more, because tenant attach already reports Intune compliance for the uploaded devices
questions.explanation: Tenant attach only provides visibility and a few remote actions; it neither enrolls the devices nor makes Intune evaluate compliance. To have Intune compliance policies drive Conditional Access, the devices need co-management with the Compliance policies workload set to Intune. Resource access policies covers items such as VPN, Wi-Fi, and certificate profiles, and Endpoint Protection covers security settings, not compliance evaluation.

questions.question: Which two requirements point to Windows 365 rather than Azure Virtual Desktop? (Choose two.)
options: Microsoft operating the underlying hosting, so no host pools or scaling plans need to be built
Multi-session Windows 11 hosts shared by many users to lower the cost per user
Pay-as-you-go billing for only the compute and storage that is consumed
Scaling session hosts down to zero outside business hours to cut compute spend
A predictable per-user monthly price regardless of how many hours the desktop is used
questions.explanation: Windows 365 is a fixed-price, per-user Cloud PC whose hosting Microsoft operates. Azure Virtual Desktop is the opposite on each of the other points: it offers multi-session hosts, scaling plans that shut hosts down when idle, and consumption-based billing, all of which the organization configures and manages itself in Azure.

questions.question: Contoso wants to eliminate password sign-in on managed Windows laptops. Each user should unlock with a PIN or biometric backed by a key stored in that laptop's TPM, not by a portable token. What should be deployed through Intune?
options: Microsoft Authenticator passwordless phone sign-in registered for each user's phone
FIDO2 security keys registered to each user's account and carried between devices
Windows Hello for Business, deployed through a device configuration or settings catalog profile
A compliance policy that requires a strong password and a short lock timeout on the laptops
questions.explanation: Windows Hello for Business replaces the password with a PIN or biometric that unlocks a key pair bound to that device's TPM, and it is deployed through an Intune profile. A FIDO2 security key is a portable token rather than a per-laptop key. Authenticator phone sign-in is a different passwordless method that does not unlock Windows with a device-bound key, and a compliance policy only checks password requirements instead of replacing the credential.

questions.question: A Windows LAPS policy backs up local administrator passwords to Microsoft Entra ID, and the passwords are rotating on the laptops. Yet technicians with the Cloud Device Administrator role see no password for any device. What is the most likely missing step?
options: Enabling the LAPS setting in the tenant's Microsoft Entra device settings
Adding the technicians to the local Administrators group on each laptop they support
Assigning an Endpoint Privilege Management elevation rule to the technicians' accounts
Changing the policy's backup directory from Entra ID to on-premises Active Directory
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra only accepts backed-up LAPS passwords when the LAPS setting is turned on in the tenant's device settings, so a deployed policy can rotate passwords locally yet have nothing to show in Entra. Technicians read the password from the directory and do not need local group membership. On-premises AD is a different backup target, and Endpoint Privilege Management elevates applications rather than exposing passwords.

questions.question: A required Win32 app installs successfully on laptops, yet Intune keeps reporting it as not installed and retries the install. The app installs per machine, but its detection rule looks for a shortcut in each user's profile that exists only after first launch. What should the admin change?
options: Replace the detection rule with a machine-level check, such as an MSI product code
Increase the app's maximum allowed install time so the installer can finish
Add a requirement rule that limits the install to the app's minimum Windows version
Change the install behavior to user so the shortcut gets created during installation
questions.explanation: Intune decides whether the app is installed by evaluating the detection rule, so a rule that depends on a user-profile shortcut never turns true after a per-machine install, and Intune keeps retrying. A machine-level check fixes that. A requirement rule only gates whether the install is attempted, switching to user context would break a per-machine installer, and a longer install time does nothing for a rule that can never be satisfied.

questions.question: Version 2.0 of a deployed Win32 app must upgrade version 1.0 in place on devices that already have it, uninstalling 1.0 first. Both apps already exist in Intune. Where should the relationship be configured?
options: On the 1.0 app, adding 2.0 as a dependency that installs before it
On the 2.0 app, adding 1.0 as a superseded app that is uninstalled first
On the 2.0 app, adding 1.0 as a dependency that installs before it
On the 1.0 app, adding 2.0 as the app that supersedes it, with uninstall enabled
questions.explanation: Supersedence is configured on the newer app, which lists the older app it replaces and can uninstall it first. A dependency means the other app must be installed before this one, so adding 2.0 as a dependency of 1.0 or 1.0 as a dependency of 2.0 builds a prerequisite chain rather than an upgrade.
