Supersedence is not set from the older app, because the relationship is defined by the replacement.

questions.question: An employee leaves. Their personal iPhone has Outlook protected by an app protection policy and was never enrolled in MDM. HR wants only the corporate data removed from Outlook, with nothing else touched. Which action should the admin use?
options: The Retire action sent from the device's page
The Fresh Start action sent from the device's page
The Wipe action sent from the device's page
An app selective wipe request for the user and device
questions.explanation: A device that is not MDM-enrolled has no device record to act on, so corporate data in a protected app is removed with an app selective wipe request for that user and device. Retire removes management and company data from an enrolled personal device, but this phone is not enrolled. Wipe would erase the whole phone, and Fresh Start is a Windows action.

questions.question: A new OEM camera driver is breaking video calls on one laptop model. IT wants to stop that one driver from installing on those laptops while other approved drivers keep installing. Which approach fits?
options: Turn off driver delivery in the update ring so no drivers install on any device in it
Create a safeguard hold for that driver so Intune blocks it on the affected laptops
Assign an expedited quality update that replaces the driver with the previous version
Use a driver update policy and withhold or pause approval for that one driver
questions.explanation: A Windows driver update policy lets an admin control drivers individually, either by approving drivers one by one or by pausing a specific driver, so the bad driver is held back while others continue. Turning off driver delivery in the ring blocks all drivers, which the scenario does not want. An expedited quality update does not roll back drivers, and safeguard holds are applied by Microsoft rather than configured by an administrator.

questions.question: An app assigned to a dynamic device group can install later than expected on a freshly provisioned device, because group membership is not evaluated instantly.
questions.explanation: Dynamic membership is evaluated on a delay, so a new device may briefly sit outside its intended group. For anything that must apply at the moment of provisioning, target an assigned group, or make sure the group tag is set before the device ships.

questions.question: A line-of-business server app needs inbound TCP 8443 opened on Windows laptops, but only while a laptop is on the corporate domain network. Which Intune policy fits?
options: A VPN profile that forwards port 8443 traffic from the corporate network to the laptops
An attack surface reduction rule that permits network connections on port 8443 from the laptops
A Microsoft Defender Firewall rules policy with an inbound allow rule for port 8443 on the Domain profile
A Microsoft Defender Firewall policy that sets the Domain profile's default inbound action to Allow for the laptops
questions.explanation: A firewall rules policy can define one inbound allow rule for a specific port and bind it to the Domain profile, so it opens only that port, only on the corporate network. Setting the Domain profile's default inbound action to Allow opens every port, which is far broader than needed. ASR rules do not manage firewall ports, and a VPN profile configures a tunnel rather than inbound firewall rules.

questions.question: Security wants Intune audit and operational logs kept for two years and queried with KQL alongside other tenant logs. Which feature delivers that?
options: Organizational reports exported on a schedule from the Reports node
An alert rule that emails log extracts to the security team each week
Diagnostic settings in Intune that send logs to a Log Analytics workspace
The Troubleshooting + support page, reviewed for each user
questions.explanation: Diagnostic settings can stream Intune audit and operational logs to a Log Analytics workspace, where retention is set on the workspace and KQL queries can join them with other logs. Organizational reports are point-in-time exports, an alert rule sends notifications rather than retaining logs, and Troubleshooting + support looks up one user's current status.

questions.question: Which two statements about feature update deployment profiles and expedited quality updates are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: A feature update deployment profile overrides the feature update deferral of a ring assigned to the same devices
An expedited quality update can install and restart a device outside its ring's deferral and active hours
Expedited quality updates are available only for devices enrolled in Windows Autopatch
An expedited update deployment can also pin devices to a specific Windows feature version instead of a fix
A feature update deployment profile replaces the quality update deferral of the ring assigned to the same devices
questions.explanation: A feature update deployment profile overrides the ring's feature deferral for its devices, and an expedited quality update is built to push an urgent fix past normal deferral and active hours. Expediting concerns quality updates and cannot pin a feature version, the profile leaves the ring's quality deferral in charge, and expediting is an Intune policy that does not require Autopatch.

questions.question: Which two statements about Win32 app relationships and the Microsoft Store app (new) type are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: Circular dependencies between Win32 apps are allowed as long as each app's detection rule differs
A Win32 app dependency is installed automatically even when the dependency app has no assignment of its own
The Microsoft Store for Business private store is still the recommended source for new store deployments
The Microsoft Store app (new) type sources apps from the public Microsoft Store and supports Required and Available
Supersedence is configured on the older app and points to the newer app that replaces it
questions.explanation: Intune installs a declared dependency as part of the deployment without it needing its own assignment, and the Microsoft Store app (new) type pulls from the public Store with the usual assignment intents. Supersedence is set on the newer app, circular dependencies are not allowed, and the Store for Business private store has been retired.

questions.question: A quality update broke a line-of-business app and reached the entire broad ring, because the pilot ring held only five IT laptops that never run that app. Which design change would have caught the problem before the broad ring received the update?
options: Raise the pilot ring's quality update deferral to 30 days so it receives updates after the broad ring does
Replace the update rings with a feature update deployment profile assigned to the whole fleet of devices
Make the earliest ring a representative sample of departments and apps, with a short deferral before later rings
Pause quality updates fleet-wide each month until IT finishes testing the line-of-business apps in a lab
questions.explanation: Staged rings only protect the fleet if the early ring is representative, so a small cross-section of departments and app sets, with a short deferral ahead of the larger rings, surfaces a regression before the broad population gets it. Deferring the pilot ring behind the broad ring defeats its purpose. A feature update profile does not stage monthly quality updates, and pausing the whole fleet delays security fixes for everyone and is only a temporary measure.

questions.question: A device is enrolled in Autopatch and eligible for Hotpatch, but it has skipped its baseline cumulative update for over four months. What is likely to happen the next time a hotpatch is released?
options: The device receives the full cumulative update with a restart, since a hotpatch applies only on a current baseline
Autopatch removes the device from its deployment ring until a baseline update is installed manually by an admin
The device is blocked from quality updates until an admin resets its Hotpatch enrollment in the admin center
The hotpatch installs in memory as normal, since hotpatches do not depend on any earlier baseline update on the device
questions.explanation: A hotpatch is a delta that applies on top of a recent baseline cumulative update, so a device that has fallen behind is offered the full cumulative update, with its restart, to get back on the baseline. The hotpatch cannot install on an out-of-date baseline, Autopatch does not drop the device from its ring, and there is no admin step to reset Hotpatch enrollment before updates resume.

questions.question: A device is hybrid Entra joined, domain-joined, and already has the Configuration Manager client installed, but it is not yet enrolled in Intune. GPO-based automatic MDM enrollment is configured tenant-wide. An administrator also enables co-management on this same device. What is the resulting state?
options: The device cannot be both Intune-enrolled and Configuration Manager-managed, so co-management fails until the Configuration Manager client is uninstalled
The device becomes Intune-enrolled, but Intune is authoritative only for workloads whose sliders were moved; the rest stay with Configuration Manager
GPO-based automatic enrollment is blocked on devices that already have the Configuration Manager client installed
Intune becomes authoritative for every workload the moment enrollment completes, whatever the slider positions are
questions.explanation: GPO-based enrollment works on a hybrid joined device regardless of the Configuration Manager client, and co-management exists precisely so that one device can be Intune-enrolled and ConfigMgr-managed at once, with each workload slider deciding which tool is authoritative for that workload. Enrollment alone does not shift any workload, the client does not have to be removed, and its presence does not block automatic enrollment.

questions.question: Contoso has 800 Windows 11 laptops that are already enrolled in Intune but were never registered for Autopilot. IT wants them to use a user-driven Autopilot deployment profile the next time they are reset, without collecting hardware hashes device by device. What should IT configure?
options: Turn on Convert all targeted devices to Autopilot in the deployment profile assigned to the laptops
Assign a dynamic device group built on a group tag to the deployment profile for the laptops
Ask the OEM to retroactively register each laptop's serial number through its partner portal account
Run a hardware hash export script on each laptop and import the combined CSV files into Intune
questions.explanation: A deployment profile can convert the Intune-managed devices it targets into Autopilot devices, which registers them without collecting hashes manually. Retroactive OEM registration is slow and depends on purchase records, a hash export script is exactly the per-device collection the scenario wants to avoid, and a group tag cannot be matched on devices that were never registered and so have no tag.

questions.question: A global company wants regional IT admins to manage only their own region's Intune devices and policies within one tenant, and regional HR admins to manage only their own region's Entra ID user accounts and licensing in that same tenant. Which pairing fits each need respectively?
options: Scope tags with scoped role assignments for Intune delegation; administrative units for Entra ID user and license delegation
Administrative units for Intune delegation; scope tags for Entra ID user and license delegation
Scope (Groups) on the Intune role assignments for both needs, since it also limits which Entra users an admin can manage
A dynamic device group per region for Intune delegation; a Conditional Access policy per region for Entra licensing
questions.explanation: Scope tags with scoped role assignments are Intune's own delegation mechanism for devices and policies, while administrative units are the Entra ID mechanism for scoping user and license administration. Swapping them applies each tool to the wrong directory. Scope (Groups) works inside Intune and does not extend to Entra user administration, and device groups and Conditional Access do not delegate administrative rights at all.

questions.question: A compliance policy marks devices noncompliant after a 5-day grace period. Security wants the user emailed the moment the device first fails a setting, and again on day 3, with no other change to the policy. What should the admin configure?
options: A notification setting inside a device configuration profile assigned to the same users
A shorter grace period on the Mark device noncompliant action, set to 0 days
Two Send email to end user actions on the policy, scheduled at 0 days and 3 days
A Conditional Access policy that emails the user when a sign-in is blocked
questions.explanation: A compliance policy accepts several noncompliance actions, each with its own schedule, so one email action at 0 days and another at 3 days run alongside the 5-day mark-noncompliant action, each using a notification message template. Conditional Access reacts at sign-in rather than when a setting fails, configuration profiles carry no compliance notifications, and a 0-day grace period would change when the device is marked noncompliant, which the scenario says to leave alone.

questions.question: A team wants standard users to run one IT-approved application that needs administrator rights, without ever granting standing local administrator access, and also wants help desk to look up a fallback local administrator password for the same machine in an emergency. Which pairing satisfies both needs without contradiction?
options: A local user group membership policy that adds the user to Administrators; Windows LAPS for the fallback password
Windows LAPS for the approved application, handing the user the rotated password only while the installer runs
Endpoint Privilege Management for both needs, since an elevation rule can also escrow a rotated local administrator password
Endpoint Privilege Management for the one approved application; Windows LAPS for the rotated local administrator password
questions.explanation: Endpoint Privilege Management elevates only the one approved application with no standing admin rights, and Windows LAPS independently manages the rotated local administrator password for emergency use, so the two are complementary. LAPS does not elevate applications for users, Endpoint Privilege Management does not manage or escrow the local administrator password, and putting the user in Administrators creates exactly the standing access the team wants to avoid.

questions.question: A Win32 app needs a runtime installed first. The runtime already exists as a separate Win32 app but has no assignment. IT wants the runtime to install before the app, and only on devices that lack it. What should IT configure?
options: Assign the runtime as Required to the All devices group so it is present everywhere
Add the runtime as an app that the main app supersedes in its relationships
Add the runtime as a dependency of the app, with automatic install enabled
Add a requirement rule to the app that checks whether the runtime is present
questions.explanation: A dependency makes Intune install the runtime first as part of deploying the app, even if the runtime has no assignment of its own, and its detection rule prevents reinstalling it where it already exists. A requirement rule only blocks the install when the runtime is missing, it does not install it. Assigning it to All devices installs it everywhere, which exceeds the need, and supersedence replaces an older version rather than supplying a prerequisite.

questions.question: A remediation's detection script correctly finds a stopped service, but the remediation script fails on devices where the service depends on a drive mapped only in the signed-in user's session. What is the most likely cause?
options: The detection and remediation scripts must share one exit code, and a mismatch makes the remediation skip
Remediation scripts run once per user, so the first failure blocks later attempts on that device until cleared
The script runs in 32-bit PowerShell by default, which cannot restart services that rely on network resources
Scripts run as SYSTEM by default and cannot see the user's mapped drive, so the remediation must run as the user
questions.explanation: Remediation scripts run in the SYSTEM context unless configured otherwise, and SYSTEM has no view of a drive mapped in a specific user's session. Setting the script to run with the logged-on user's credentials resolves that. A shared exit code is not required, the 32-bit versus 64-bit setting does not affect access to mapped drives, and remediations are scheduled to run repeatedly rather than once per user.

questions.question: A branch office has 150 PCs on a slow WAN link that all download the same large updates. Which two statements about using Delivery Optimization to ease the load are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: HTTP-only mode lets branch devices peer over the local network while still falling back to Microsoft
Each branch needs a Configuration Manager distribution point before its devices can peer with one another
LAN download mode limits peering to devices on the local network, keeping shared content inside the branch
Peers can share Win32 app content deployed through Intune, not just Windows updates
Delivery Optimization applies to Windows quality updates only, so feature updates and apps still download individually
questions.explanation: Delivery Optimization also serves Win32 and Microsoft Store app content, and LAN mode keeps peering on the local network, which is why it suits a branch with a constrained WAN link. No Configuration Manager distribution point is needed for peering. It is not limited to quality updates, and HTTP-only mode disables peering altogether, so every device would download from Microsoft individually.

questions.question: An admin tries to enroll new iPads through Automated Device Enrollment, but every attempt fails. At the same time, iPhones already managed by Intune have stopped receiving MDM commands. What is the most likely cause?
options: The Apple Push Notification service (APNs) certificate has expired and must be renewed under the original Apple ID
The VPP token that Intune uses for app licensing has expired and must be renewed in the admin center
The Apple Business Manager server token used for Automated Device Enrollment has expired and needs renewing
A platform enrollment restriction is blocking iOS/iPadOS enrollment for the users in the tenant
questions.explanation: An expired APNs certificate stops Intune from pushing MDM commands to every enrolled Apple device and blocks new Apple enrollment at the same time, which matches both symptoms. An expired Automated Device Enrollment token would break new ADE enrollment and sync but not commands to enrolled iPhones, an expired VPP token affects only app licensing, and an enrollment restriction blocks new enrollments without touching devices that are already managed.

questions.question: Regional HR admins must be able to reset passwords for users in their own region only, and must have no Intune permissions at all. What should be configured?
options: Scope (Groups) on an Intune role assignment that lists each region's user group
The Password Administrator role assigned at tenant scope, with a Conditional Access policy limiting which users it covers
A scope tag per region, with the Intune Help Desk Operator role assigned to the HR admins at that tag
An administrative unit per region holding that region's users, with the Password Administrator role scoped to it
questions.explanation: An administrative unit scopes a directory role such as Password Administrator to only the users inside it, which is directory-level delegation with no Intune rights implied. A scope tag with an Intune role does the opposite, granting Intune permissions and limiting only Intune objects. A tenant-scoped role covers every user, and Conditional Access cannot narrow an administrator's role. Scope (Groups) exists only on Intune role assignments.

questions.question: Security wants Microsoft Defender to hold an unknown file from running while Microsoft's cloud analyzes it, accepting a short delay. Which setting should be configured?
options: Network protection in block mode for outbound connections
Cloud-delivered protection with a higher cloud block level
Controlled folder access in block mode for the user's folders
Potentially unwanted application protection in block mode
questions.explanation: Cloud-delivered protection with a higher cloud block level is the setting that checks suspicious files against Microsoft's cloud intelligence and can hold a file while the verdict is pending, at the cost of a little latency. PUA protection blocks adware-type software, controlled folder access protects designated folders from untrusted apps, and network protection blocks connections to low-reputation destinations, so none of them analyze unknown files in the cloud.

questions.question: A help-desk technician was added to the local Administrators group on a managed laptop outside any approved process. The approved members are a break-glass account and the IT-Ops group. Intune should remove anyone else from that group at every policy evaluation. What should be deployed?
options: A local user group membership policy for Administrators that replaces membership with the approved accounts
An Endpoint Privilege Management elevation settings policy that denies elevation requests from standard users
A Windows LAPS policy that rotates the break-glass account's password on a schedule
The same policy configured to add the approved accounts to the Administrators group but not remove others
questions.explanation: The Account protection local user group membership policy can replace a group's membership with a defined list, so anyone added outside the policy is removed at the next evaluation. The same policy set only to add approved accounts leaves unapproved members in place. LAPS rotates the password of an existing administrator account rather than deciding who belongs to the group, and Endpoint Privilege Management governs application elevation, not group membership.

questions.question: A hospital buys App Store apps for 400 shared, corporate-owned iPads. Nurses never sign in with personal Apple IDs, and the apps must install silently as soon as a device enrolls. Which licensing approach fits?
options: User-licensed VPP apps assigned to the nurses' user group
iOS store apps without a VPP token, set as Available in the Company Portal
Line-of-business .ipa files uploaded to Intune and signed with an enterprise certificate
Device-licensed VPP apps with a Required assignment to the iPads' device group
questions.explanation: Device licensing ties an App Store license to the device, so no Apple ID is needed and a Required assignment can install silently at enrollment. User licensing ties each license to a person's Apple ID, which nurses on shared devices do not use. Available apps wait for a user to choose them, and an .ipa upload is for in-house apps, not for App Store apps.

questions.question: A Win32 app shows a successful install status for every targeted device, but one department reports that the app's shortcut never appears on their Start menu, although the files are on disk. The installer registers shortcuts per signed-in user. What is the most likely cause?
options: The app's requirement rule checks for a user-profile path that appears after the first sign-in
The app was assigned as Available instead of Required, so the shortcut step waits for the user to click Install
The app was deployed with install behavior set to System, which suits per-machine installers but not this one
The detection rule checks the installation folder, so Intune reports success even though the installer failed
questions.explanation: An installer that registers shortcuts per user needs the user context. Run as System, it completes under SYSTEM, the files land and detection passes, but nothing registers for any signed-in user. A requirement rule would stop the install attempt altogether rather than skip one step, the installer did not fail since the files are present, and an Available assignment would show no install status without a user choosing it.

questions.question: A user's laptop shows a failed Win32 app install with a vague error. The user is on a call. The admin needs the device's logs and event data without touching the device or asking the user to export anything. What should the admin do?
options: Send a Sync action to the device and read the refreshed install status afterward
Run Collect diagnostics on the device and download the package when it finishes
Review the app's install status and error code on the Troubleshooting + support page
Run Fresh Start with the option to keep user data, then read the new logs
questions.explanation: Collect diagnostics gathers logs and configuration state remotely into a package the admin downloads, without changing the device or interrupting the user. The Troubleshooting + support page shows status and error codes but not the device's logs, Sync only prompts a check-in, and Fresh Start reinstalls Windows, which is disruptive and not diagnostic.

questions.question: A supervised corporate iPad is missing, and it may simply be in another building. The admin wants it locked with a contact message on the screen and wants to see its location, without erasing anything. Which action fits?
options: Send the Wipe action while keeping enrollment
Send the Retire action
Enable Lost Mode, then use Locate device
Send the Remote lock action
questions.explanation: Lost Mode on a supervised iOS or iPadOS device locks it, shows a message and phone number, and allows the device to be located, all without erasing data. Remote lock secures the device but shows no message and gives no location. Retire and Wipe both remove data or management, which is premature for a device that might be found.

questions.question: An admin needs an update-focused view of feature and quality update deployment status and deadlines, and wants to query it with KQL to build custom workbooks. What should the admin use?
options: Organizational reports exported as a CSV from the Reports node
Intune's built-in Windows feature update report in the Reports node
Intune diagnostic settings that stream audit and operational logs to Log Analytics
Windows Update for Business reports, backed by a Log Analytics workspace
questions.explanation: Windows Update for Business reports is the update-specific workbook backed by Log Analytics, so its deployment data can be queried with KQL. The built-in Intune update report offers fixed views without KQL, diagnostic settings stream Intune audit and operational logs that do not hold update deployment status, and organizational reports are exportable datasets rather than a queryable update workbook.

questions.question: Which two configurations are required for a user-driven Windows Autopilot deployment that must hybrid Microsoft Entra join new laptops? (Choose two.)
options: A self-deploying Autopilot profile with the hybrid join option selected
The Intune Connector for Active Directory installed on a domain-joined server
A Microsoft Entra registered record created in advance for each laptop
A Domain Join configuration profile that names the domain and the target OU
An Autopilot device preparation policy assigned to the laptops' device group
questions.explanation: Hybrid join through Autopilot needs the Intune Connector for Active Directory to create the computer object on-premises, and a Domain Join profile that tells it which domain and OU to use. Self-deploying profiles support Microsoft Entra join only, device preparation also supports only Entra join, and the laptops do not need a pre-created registered record.

questions.question: The jailbroken or rooted device check in an app protection policy's conditional launch settings applies only to devices that are enrolled in MDM.
questions.explanation: App protection policies work at the app level, so conditional launch can block or wipe the app on a jailbroken or rooted device whether or not the device is enrolled. Enrollment is not required.

questions.question: An admin tries to add a public app to an Android Enterprise assignment in Intune, but the app picker offers no catalog of apps. What should be done first?
options: Create an app protection policy that targets Android apps
Enroll a test device through Android device administrator mode first
Create an app configuration policy that targets the Android apps
Connect the tenant to Managed Google Play from the Intune admin center
questions.explanation: Android Enterprise app distribution depends on the one-time connection between the tenant and Managed Google Play, which provides the catalog that apps are approved and assigned from. An app configuration policy and an app protection policy both act on an app that is already available, and a device administrator enrollment is a legacy path that does not provide the catalog.

questions.question: The Wipe action always keeps a Windows device's Microsoft Entra join and Intune enrollment so it can be reissued straight away.
questions.explanation: Wipe has an option to retain enrollment state and user account, but it is a choice rather than a given. Without it the device is reset and loses its enrollment.

questions.question: A company deploys certificate-based Wi-Fi to managed Windows laptops. Which two statements are correct? (Choose two.)
options: The SCEP certificate profile references a trusted certificate profile that delivers the root CA to the devices
A Wi-Fi profile that uses EAP-TLS issues the device's client certificate by itself during connection
The Wi-Fi profile references the certificate profile that supplies the client certificate used to authenticate
The trusted certificate profile can be skipped because Windows trusts the CA behind an installed client certificate
Certificate-based Wi-Fi works with Microsoft Cloud PKI as the issuer but not with SCEP or PKCS certificates
questions.explanation: A SCEP profile points at a trusted certificate profile for the root CA, and the Wi-Fi profile points at the certificate profile to use for client authentication, so the pieces must be assigned together. A Wi-Fi profile does not issue certificates, Windows does not automatically trust the issuing CA without the root being delivered, and SCEP, PKCS, and Cloud PKI can all supply the certificate.

questions.question: Which three statements about Apple VPP licensing and Managed Google Play in Intune are accurate? (Choose three.)
options: A VPP license can be reclaimed and reassigned after the app is removed from a device
Managed Google Play requires a personal Google account on a fully managed corporate device before any app installs
Managed Google Play must be linked to the tenant once before Android Enterprise apps can be assigned
Device-licensed VPP apps install on a device without any Apple ID being signed in
User-licensed VPP apps can be assigned directly to a device group without any user involved
questions.explanation: Device licensing needs no Apple ID on the device, a one-time Managed Google Play connection is the prerequisite for Android Enterprise apps, and VPP licenses can be reclaimed and reassigned through Intune. User licenses are tied to people, so they are assigned to users, and a fully managed device does not need a personal Google account.

questions.question: Which three statements about Intune remote actions are accurate? (Choose three.)
options: Collect diagnostics leaves the device unchanged and returns its logs for download in the admin center
Retire removes company data, apps, and management from a device while leaving the user's personal data in place
Fresh Start keeps the OEM-installed apps while it removes the user's data from the device
Remote lock requires the admin to choose a new passcode for the user before the device locks
Wipe can retain the device's enrollment state and user account, so it is reprovisioned without re-enrolling
questions.explanation: Collect diagnostics only gathers logs, Wipe can retain enrollment and the user account for reprovisioning, and Retire strips company data, apps, and management while leaving personal data alone. Remote lock secures the device without setting a passcode, and Fresh Start exists mainly to remove OEM-installed apps rather than keep them.

questions.question: An attacker with local administrator rights on a managed laptop tries to switch off Microsoft Defender Antivirus real-time protection from the device itself. Which control is designed to stop that local change?
options: Controlled folder access in block mode for user documents
A higher cloud block level in the Antivirus policy
An attack surface reduction rule that blocks credential stealing from LSASS
Tamper protection, enabled through the Antivirus policy
questions.explanation: Tamper protection locks core Defender Antivirus settings, such as real-time protection, against local changes even by a user with administrator rights. Controlled folder access protects folders from untrusted apps, the LSASS rule blocks one credential-theft behavior, and a higher cloud block level tightens detection, but none of them stop an administrator from turning protection off.

questions.question: Threat intelligence names a domain used for command and control. Security creates a URL/domain indicator in block mode for onboarded Windows laptops, but the devices can still reach the domain. What else must be enabled?
options: Tamper protection on the laptops, so Defender settings resist local changes
Network protection in block mode, with custom network indicators enabled in the portal
A higher cloud block level in the Antivirus policy, with sample submission turned on
Controlled folder access in block mode on the onboarded laptops, with its own exclusions list
questions.explanation: Indicators for URLs, domains, and IP addresses are enforced through network protection, so it must run in block mode on the devices, and custom network indicators must be turned on in the Defender portal. Controlled folder access, the cloud block level, and tamper protection are separate protections that do not enforce network indicators.

questions.question: A factory needs most USB drives blocked, but a small set of IT-issued drives, identified by hardware ID, must keep working. What should be configured?
options: A compliance policy that marks devices noncompliant when removable storage is attached to them
A BitLocker To Go requirement that forces encryption on removable drives before they can be written to
The attack surface reduction rule that blocks untrusted and unsigned processes from running on USB drives
A device control policy with approved hardware IDs in a reusable group, allowed ahead of a default deny rule
questions.explanation: A device control policy can allow a defined set of hardware IDs while denying other removable storage, which is the allow-list behavior the factory needs. The ASR rule only restricts untrusted processes launched from USB and does not decide which drives mount. A compliance policy reports a finding without blocking the drive, and BitLocker To Go requires encryption rather than limiting which devices are allowed.

questions.question: Which two requirements mean an app must be packaged as a Win32 app rather than uploaded as a line-of-business app? (Choose two.)
options: The package is an MSIX file that is distributed internally
The installer is a single MSI that installs silently with default settings
A newer version must automatically replace the older one through supersedence
The app needs a runtime installed first through a dependency relationship
The app must be assigned as Required to a device group
questions.explanation: Dependencies and supersedence are features of Win32 apps, which is the trade-off for the extra .intunewin packaging step. A single MSI with default switches, a Required assignment, and an MSIX package are all supported by line-of-business apps, so none of them forces the Win32 type.

questions.question: Which two requirements are configured under conditional launch in an app protection policy? (Choose two.)
options: Require the PIN again after 30 minutes of inactivity in the app
Block access when the device's OS version is below a minimum
Block saving corporate files to personal storage locations
Restrict cut, copy, and paste between managed and unmanaged apps
Wipe corporate data once the app has been offline past a set period
questions.explanation: Conditional launch holds the conditions that are checked when the app starts, such as a minimum OS version and the offline grace period, with an action to block or wipe. The PIN inactivity timeout belongs to access requirements, and cut-copy-paste and save-as restrictions belong to data protection.

questions.question: Contoso's app-compatibility team validates Microsoft 365 Apps updates once a month and cannot absorb unpredictable mid-month feature drops, but waiting six months between releases is too slow. Which update channel fits?
options: Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel
Current Channel (Preview)
Monthly Enterprise Channel
Current Channel
questions.explanation: Monthly Enterprise Channel delivers feature updates once a month on a predictable date, which matches a team that validates monthly. Current Channel ships features as they are ready, so the date is unpredictable, and the Preview channel is meant for early testing. Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel waits about six months between feature releases, which the team calls too slow.

questions.question: IT holds the premium Intune add-on for app management. It wants Microsoft-prepackaged, regularly updated versions of common apps, without building .intunewin packages or writing detection rules. Which app source should IT choose?
options: An Enterprise App Catalog app
A line-of-business app uploaded as an MSI
The Microsoft Store app (new) type
A Win32 app prepared with the Content Prep Tool
questions.explanation: The Enterprise App Catalog provides apps that Microsoft has already packaged, complete with install commands and detection rules, and adds new versions as they are published. The Microsoft Store app (new) type only offers what the Store carries, a Win32 app needs IT to build the package and rules, and a line-of-business MSI also leaves the packaging and maintenance to IT.

questions.question: Front-desk PCs should drop users straight into their Cloud PC at the Windows sign-in screen. Laptop users already signed in to their local desktop should be able to move to their Cloud PC from the taskbar without signing out. Which pairing of capabilities fits, respectively?
options: Windows 365 Boot for the front-desk PCs and for the laptops
Windows 365 Frontline (now Windows 365 Flex) for the front-desk PCs; Windows 365 Switch for the laptops
Windows 365 Boot for the front-desk PCs; Windows 365 Switch for the laptops
Windows 365 Switch for the front-desk PCs; Windows 365 Boot for the laptops
questions.explanation: Windows 365 Boot changes how a session starts, signing the user in at the lock screen straight into the Cloud PC, which matches the front desk. Windows 365 Switch moves a user between the local desktop and the Cloud PC from within a signed-in session, which matches the laptops. Reversing them swaps the two behaviors, Frontline is a licensing model rather than a sign-in experience, and Boot alone would not give laptop users a way to move back and forth without signing out.

questions.question: Contoso blocks personally owned iOS devices with a platform enrollment restriction. Procurement bought 50 iPhones at retail that must enroll as corporate-owned anyway. Which setting lets them enroll?
options: Raise the device limit restriction for the users who will receive them
Add a higher-priority platform restriction that allows personal iOS devices for those users
Assign a Corporate device category to the 50 iPhones before they enroll
Upload their serial numbers as corporate device identifiers
questions.explanation: Corporate device identifiers mark specific hardware, by serial number or IMEI, as corporate-owned at enrollment, so the personal-device block does not apply and the ownership value is correct afterward. A device limit restriction counts devices rather than ownership. A higher-priority allow rule would let those users enroll personal devices too and would record the iPhones as personal, and a device category is a purpose label that does not affect ownership or the restriction.

questions.question: Refurbished laptops, previously used unencrypted, are being reissued. Compliance requires that no recoverable remnants of earlier deleted data remain once BitLocker is on. Which Intune BitLocker choice meets that?
options: Full disk encryption, which also encrypts the empty sectors
Used space only encryption, which finishes faster on previously used drives
A stronger cipher such as XTS-AES 256, which also encrypts free space
A TPM plus PIN startup requirement, which wipes deleted data at first boot
questions.explanation: Full disk encryption also encrypts empty sectors, so remnants of earlier deleted data are not left readable in free space, which matters for a drive that held data before BitLocker. Used space only encrypts just the sectors holding data and is faster, so it can leave old traces. The cipher strength changes how data is encrypted, not which sectors, and a startup PIN controls unlock rather than wiping anything.

questions.question: Auditors want cached domain credentials kept in a hardware-backed, virtualization-isolated enclave, so even malware running as local administrator cannot read them from memory. Which control meets that requirement?
options: The attack surface reduction rule that blocks credential stealing from LSASS
Credential Guard, turned on through an endpoint security profile
Windows Hello for Business with a TPM-bound key
LSA protection, which runs the LSASS process as a protected process
questions.explanation: Credential Guard uses virtualization-based security to isolate cached domain credentials in an enclave that the operating system itself cannot read. The ASR rule blocks a behavior but leaves credentials in LSASS memory, LSA protection hardens the LSASS process without moving secrets out of it, and Windows Hello for Business changes how users authenticate rather than isolating credentials that are already cached.

questions.question: A Win32 app assigned as Required to a device group installs even when no user is signed in to the device.
questions.explanation: A device-targeted required app installs in the system context, so it does not wait for anyone to sign in. A user-targeted assignment is what waits for a user.

questions.question: An app protection policy applies to a user who has no Intune license, as long as the device is unenrolled.
questions.explanation: Enrollment is not what licenses the policy. The user needs an Intune license for app protection to apply, so an unlicensed user does not receive it even on an unenrolled device.

questions.question: A hospital opens a new clinic that needs the same 12 apps, 5 profiles, and compliance policy that every other clinic already has. IT wants to assign the whole bundle once instead of one item at a time. What should IT use?
options: An assignment filter added to each existing item
A scope tag created for the new clinic
A security baseline that includes the apps and profiles
A policy set assigned to the new clinic's group
questions.explanation: A policy set bundles apps, configuration profiles, and compliance policies into one object that is assigned to a group in a single step. A security baseline contains only security settings, not apps, an assignment filter narrows individual assignments and still needs each item assigned, and a scope tag controls which admins can see an object.

questions.question: Autopilot Reset removes a device's Microsoft Entra join and Intune enrollment, so the device must go through full enrollment again at the next out-of-box experience.
questions.explanation: Autopilot Reset wipes personal data, apps, and settings but keeps the device's connection to Microsoft Entra ID and its management connection to Intune, then reapplies provisioning. That is why it is the fast way to reissue a device without repeating enrollment.

questions.question: Which two statements about tamper protection and Defender for Endpoint indicators are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: A URL indicator in block mode is enforced even when network protection is turned off on the device
A file indicator in block mode relies on Defender Antivirus with cloud-delivered protection turned on
Indicators can be created for files only, not for IP addresses, URLs, domains, or certificates
Tamper protection blocks local changes to protected Defender settings, yet Intune policy changes still apply
Tamper protection prevents Intune from changing Defender Antivirus settings on the devices it protects
questions.explanation: Tamper protection stops local edits, including by an administrator, yet centrally managed Intune changes still apply, and file indicators are enforced by Defender Antivirus with cloud-delivered protection on. URL and domain indicators depend on network protection, tamper protection does not stop Intune, and indicators also cover IP addresses, URLs and domains, and certificates.

questions.question: Which two statements about packaging and installing Intune apps are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: The Intune Management Extension must be installed manually before the first Win32 app can be assigned
An MSI uploaded as a line-of-business app supports custom requirement rules and supersedence
A Win32 app's detection rule is optional whenever a requirement rule is defined
The Win32 Content Prep Tool produces an encrypted .intunewin file that must be created for each new version of a Win32 app
Microsoft 365 Apps are deployed with their own Intune app type and do not need to be packaged as a Win32 app
questions.explanation: Each Win32 app version needs a freshly prepared .intunewin package, and Microsoft 365 Apps have a dedicated app type. Line-of-business MSI apps lack custom requirement rules and supersedence, the Intune Management Extension installs itself when a Win32 app or script is assigned, and a detection rule is mandatory for every Win32 app.

questions.question: Contoso issues Android phones to 300 delivery drivers. The phones are company-owned, each is assigned to one driver, IT wants full control of the whole device, and drivers must not be able to add personal accounts. Which Android Enterprise enrollment option should the admin use?
options: Personally owned devices with a work profile, so personal and work data stay separate
Corporate-owned dedicated (COSU) devices, because every phone is used for one business purpose
Android device administrator, which gives the broadest control on every Android version
Corporate-owned fully managed (COBO)
questions.explanation: Fully managed enrollment is for company-owned devices assigned to a user, where Intune manages the whole device. A personal work profile separates data on devices the user owns and leaves the rest of the phone alone. Dedicated devices are user-less kiosks or shared devices, which does not match phones assigned to individual drivers. Device administrator is a legacy mode that offers less control on current Android versions and is not the recommended option.
questions.whyTested: Enrollment questions hinge on ownership and whether a user is attached to the device: BYOD is work profile, corporate with a user is fully managed or COPE, and user-less is dedicated.

questions.question: A user reports that her new personal iPhone will not enroll. The enrollment failures report shows reason "device limit reached" for her account. Other users enroll fine. What should the admin check?
options: Whether the Apple Push Notification service certificate has expired for the whole tenant and every Apple device
Whether the Intune Connector for Active Directory is installed on a domain-joined server
Whether the iPhone has first been registered in Windows Autopilot by its hardware hash
The device limit restriction that applies to her, and how many devices she already has enrolled
questions.explanation: A device limit restriction caps how many devices one user can enroll; the failure reason in the enrollment failures report points directly at it, so the admin raises the limit or removes an old device. An expired Apple Push Notification certificate would affect every Apple enrollment, not one user. The Active Directory connector concerns hybrid Windows devices, and Autopilot registration is a Windows-only process.

questions.question: A Windows 365 admin must let a colleague view Cloud PC provisioning policies, images, and Cloud PCs in the Intune admin center, but not change anything. Which role fits?
options: Intune Administrator
Windows 365 Network Interface Contributor
Cloud PC Reader
Cloud PC Administrator
questions.explanation: Cloud PC Reader is a built-in read-only role for the Windows 365 node. Cloud PC Administrator manages images, network connections, and provisioning, which means it can change things. The Windows 365 Network Interface Contributor role is a role the Windows 365 service receives on the Azure network connection's resource group, not an admin role. Intune Administrator is far broader than needed.

questions.question: Cloud PCs must reach an on-premises file server and use Group Policy objects that cannot be converted to Intune. Which provisioning approach is required?
options: A gallery image with Microsoft 365 Apps preinstalled, which adds on-premises connectivity
An Azure network connection with line of sight to on-premises, using hybrid Microsoft Entra join
The Microsoft-hosted network with Microsoft Entra join, which also reaches on-premises Active Directory
The Microsoft-hosted network with hybrid Microsoft Entra join, which Microsoft manages for you
questions.explanation: Hybrid Microsoft Entra join requires the Azure network connection option, because the Microsoft-hosted network is a cloud-only deployment with no connectivity to on-premises Active Directory. The image content has no effect on network reachability.

questions.question: A security review of an Intune tenant finds that new Windows devices can be used by employees without ever being enrolled. The auditors reference Zero Trust recommendations. Which tenant setting addresses this?
options: Add scope tags to every device configuration profile in the tenant
Create a compliance policy that is assigned only to the Android devices
Turn on enrollment notifications that are sent only to administrators
Enforce Windows automatic enrollment so devices joining Entra ID enroll
questions.explanation: Automatic MDM enrollment makes Windows devices that join Microsoft Entra ID enroll in Intune, so unmanaged endpoints are not left outside management and compliance. Notifications and scope tags help awareness and delegation but do not enroll anything. An Android-only compliance policy does not touch Windows devices.

questions.question: Which two statements about Windows 365 Cloud PC provisioning are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: The Microsoft-hosted network can reach on-premises Active Directory directly
A Cloud PC needs an Azure network connection to be hybrid Microsoft Entra joined
A custom image can be a multi-session image
A custom image must be generation 2 and generalized
questions.explanation: Custom images must be generation 2, generalized, single-session images, and hybrid join requires an Azure network connection. Multi-session images are not supported, and the Microsoft-hosted network has no line of sight to on-premises Active Directory.

questions.question: Contoso uses user-driven Autopilot with Microsoft Entra join. Help desk wants every laptop named with the prefix LT- followed by the serial number. Serial numbers are never longer than 12 characters. What should the admin do?
options: LT-%SERIAL%-%RAND:6% so that every name is guaranteed to be unique
Rename the devices with a platform script after the user first signs in to Windows
A template that fits in 15 characters, such as LT-%SERIAL%
Configure the name in the domain join profile only, since name templates require hybrid join
questions.explanation: A device name template is limited to 15 characters and supports %SERIAL% and %RAND:x%; it requires Microsoft Entra join. LT- plus a 12-character serial is exactly 15 characters, which fits, while adding a random part would exceed the limit. Hybrid join profiles only accept a prefix. A script after sign-in is unnecessary and renames late in the process.
questions.whyTested: The 15 character cap is the trap: the template looks fine until macros expand.

questions.question: A company needs to deploy new laptops that are hybrid Microsoft Entra joined, with a technician pre-provisioning them at a depot before shipping. Which Autopilot approach should it choose?
options: Windows Autopilot device preparation in user-driven mode with hybrid join
Windows Autopilot device preparation in automatic mode
A classic Windows Autopilot deployment profile in pre-provisioning mode
A self-deploying profile with the Enrollment Status Page disabled
questions.explanation: Device preparation supports Microsoft Entra join only, and it has no technician pre-provisioning flow, so a scenario with hybrid join and pre-provisioning needs classic profiles. A self-deploying profile does not include a technician phase and disabling the ESP is not related to the requirement.

questions.question: An admin creates a feature update policy targeting Windows 11. Several Windows 10 laptops in the group do not meet Windows 11 hardware requirements and should still receive the newest Windows 10 feature update. Which approach avoids a second policy?
options: Wait for each ineligible device to be dropped from the group automatically by Intune
Edit the existing policy later to add the Windows 10 fallback once the first deployment completes
Select the option to install the latest Windows 10 feature update on devices not capable of Windows 11
Create a dynamic group of ineligible devices and assign them an update ring with a 0-day deferral
questions.explanation: The policy option installs the latest Windows 10 feature update on ineligible devices, so one policy covers both groups. The option has to be chosen when the policy is created, because editing it later ends the current deployment and starts two new ones. An update ring deferral does not offer a feature update, and devices are not removed from groups automatically.

questions.question: Contoso wants employees who replace their laptops to see their personalized Windows settings and Microsoft Store app list restored during the out-of-box experience on the new device. New devices use user-driven Autopilot with Microsoft Entra join. What must the admin configure?
options: Backup and restore policies for Windows settings backup and restore, with restore enabled for enrollment
A self-deploying Autopilot profile, because it restores user data without any sign-in
A Windows 365 Boot guided scenario for the new laptops, so settings follow the user
Enterprise State Roaming only, configured for each device group in Entra ID
questions.explanation: Windows settings backup and restore (formerly Windows Backup for Organizations) is off by default; admins configure backup policy and enable restore, either in the tenant-wide enrollment setting or a settings catalog policy. OOBE restore requires a user-driven Autopilot profile, so a self-deploying profile does not work. Windows 365 Boot is for connecting to a Cloud PC, and Enterprise State Roaming management has moved into this feature.

questions.question: A warehouse runs Zebra handheld scanners enrolled as Android Enterprise dedicated devices. They need Zebra-specific settings that the standard Android profiles do not expose. What should the admin deploy?
options: A custom OMA-URI profile that sets Zebra configuration service provider paths
An OEMConfig profile using the Zebra OEMConfig app approved in managed Google Play
A Windows Autopilot deployment profile assigned to the Zebra scanners
An app protection policy that targets the scanner firmware and operating system
questions.explanation: Manufacturer-specific settings on Android Enterprise devices are delivered with OEMConfig, using the OEM's OEMConfig app (for Zebra, Zebra OEMConfig Powered by MX on newer Android versions). OMA-URI profiles are for Windows and some Apple settings, Autopilot is for Windows, and app protection policies protect app data, not device firmware.

questions.question: Contractors use their personal, unenrolled iPhones and Android phones. Security wants them to reach an on-premises web app only through a corporate VPN gateway, with Conditional Access still applied, and without enrolling the devices. Which Intune capability fits?
options: Microsoft Tunnel for MAM, which extends the Tunnel gateway to unenrolled devices
A Wi-Fi configuration profile assigned to the contractors' own personal devices
A SCEP certificate profile deployed to the contractors' phones for VPN sign-in
A device compliance policy that requires enrollment before the VPN can be used
questions.explanation: Tunnel for MAM extends the existing Microsoft Tunnel gateway to Android and iOS devices that are not enrolled in Intune, through managed apps. Wi-Fi profiles and SCEP certificates need enrolled devices, and a compliance policy that requires enrollment defeats the BYOD goal.

questions.question: A school district must wipe 90 student tablets at the end of term from the Intune admin center without selecting each device one by one. Which approach is appropriate?
options: The Retire action, because only retire is supported in bulk device actions
Devices > All devices > Bulk device actions, selecting up to 100 devices
A compliance policy with an action that wipes devices automatically on a chosen date
Deleting the Microsoft Entra security group that holds all of the student devices
questions.explanation: Bulk device actions support up to 100 devices at a time and include wipe. Compliance actions for noncompliance do not wipe on a date, retire is not the only bulk action, and deleting a group does not wipe the devices.

questions.question: During a call a help-desk technician reads a BitLocker recovery key aloud to a user. Security wants that key invalidated immediately, without touching the user's device. What should the admin do?
options: Wipe the device so that a new key is generated during the next enrollment
Run the BitLocker key rotation action from the device page
Reset the user's password in Microsoft Entra ID so old secrets stop working
Disable BitLocker on the device and then enable it again at a later date
questions.explanation: The BitLocker key rotation remote action generates a new recovery key for the OS drive and escrows it, so the old key is useless. Wiping or decrypting the device is far more disruptive, and a password reset does not change BitLocker keys.

questions.question: A laptop's built-in administrator password was shared with a vendor during a support session. The device is Entra joined and its Windows LAPS password already backs up to Microsoft Entra ID. What is the quickest way to change the password right now?
options: Run the Rotate local admin password remote action
Wait for the next scheduled password age to expire under the LAPS policy
Re-enroll the device in Intune so that the account is recreated
Remove the Windows LAPS policy from the device so it generates a new one
questions.explanation: The rotate local admin password action forces a new password outside the LAPS schedule for corporate-owned Windows devices that already back up to Microsoft Entra ID. Waiting leaves the old password valid, and removing the policy or re-enrolling does not rotate it.

questions.question: Apple ADE devices enroll, but required apps and policies assigned to a dynamic group arrive late because group membership evaluation lags behind setup. The admin wants the device in a security group already during enrollment. Which feature should be used?
options: Enrollment time grouping in the Apple enrollment policy
A scope tag that is added to the enrollment profile
Device categories that are chosen by the user in the Company Portal
An assignment filter that is applied to the app assignment
questions.explanation: Enrollment time grouping assigns the device to a specified Microsoft Entra security group during enrollment so group-targeted content applies earlier in setup. Assignment filters narrow a deployment but do not add group membership. Scope tags control admin visibility, and categories rely on the user acting after enrollment.

questions.question: Contoso manages iPads and Macs. It wants all devices to install the newest OS 14 days after release at 02:00, without sending update commands from Intune. Which setup fits?
options: A settings catalog Declarative Device Management policy: enforce latest, 14 days delay, 02:00 install time
A custom compliance policy that checks the operating system version of each device
An old MDM-based iOS update policy with a scheduled install window and push command
An update ring with a 14-day quality update deferral for Apple devices
questions.explanation: Apple update policies now use Declarative Device Management in the settings catalog: the Latest version model uses a delay in days and an install time, and devices enforce it themselves. The MDM-based update policies are deprecated. Update rings are for Windows, and a compliance policy only reports state.

questions.question: Contoso manages corporate-owned Samsung and Zebra devices in a warehouse and wants firmware updates delivered to devices without user action, scheduled outside shifts. Which approach should the admin use?
options: A Wi-Fi profile that forces the devices to download the latest firmware
An app protection policy with conditional launch set to the minimum OS version
A Windows feature update deployment profile assigned to the warehouse device group
FOTA updates with the Samsung Knox E-FOTA and Zebra LifeGuard OTA integrations
questions.explanation: FOTA management is available for corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices through manufacturer integrations (Samsung E-FOTA, Zebra LifeGuard OTA), with scheduling; it needs Intune Plan 2. The other options are Windows update, app-level, or connectivity features and do not control firmware.

questions.question: A technician needs to roll a new compliance policy to a fleet in stages: a pilot ring first, then 25 percent of devices after three days, then everyone. The admin wants a reusable rollout pattern for other payloads too. Which Intune capability is designed for this?
options: A scope tag created for each ring, applied to the compliance policy
Deployment plans, which define rings with deferral days between them
Device categories with automatic group membership for each ring
Policy sets, which bundle payloads together for a single assignment
questions.explanation: Deployment plans (currently in public preview) are reusable templates that define rings of group assignments with deferrals between them, applied to an app or policy through a deployment. Policy sets bundle items but do not stage them over time, categories do not time anything, and scope tags only control visibility.

questions.question: Teams reports Windows 11 laptops running very old Microsoft Defender Antivirus definitions after a long outage. The admin wants to refresh the definitions on one device immediately from Intune. Which action should be used?
options: The Autopilot Reset action on that single device
The Fresh Start action, which reinstalls Windows on that device
The Update Windows Defender security intelligence remote action
The Wipe action, followed by re-enrollment of the device
questions.explanation: The security intelligence update action tells the device to refresh Microsoft Defender Antivirus definitions immediately. Wipe, Autopilot Reset, and Fresh Start reset or reinstall the device and are not proportionate.

questions.question: Windows 365 admins want new Cloud PCs for developers to start from a preconfigured image that already contains Microsoft 365 Apps and Teams optimizations, with no image building. Where should they get it?
options: A generation 1 image with a recovery partition
The gallery images offered when creating the provisioning policy
A custom image captured from a multi-session Azure Virtual Desktop host
An image that contains FSLogix profile containers pre-installed
questions.explanation: The Windows 365 gallery offers images with Microsoft 365 Apps preinstalled (and Teams optimizations) that are updated monthly, so no custom image is needed. Custom images cannot be multi-session, cannot contain FSLogix components, must not have a recovery partition, and new ones must be generation 2.

questions.question: Windows Autopilot device preparation can hybrid Microsoft Entra join a device.
questions.explanation: Device preparation supports Microsoft Entra join only. Hybrid join requires a classic Autopilot deployment profile together with the domain join configuration.

questions.question: Windows settings backup and restore requires admins to configure backup policy, because backup is not turned on automatically on Windows 11 versions earlier than 26H2.
questions.explanation: The feature is opt-in until an admin configures it; Windows 11 version 26H2 changes the default so backup is enabled by default on eligible devices, but admin-set policy is still honored and restore still has to be configured.

questions.question: Which two statements about Intune remote actions are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: Rotate local admin password works only when Windows LAPS is already backing the password up to Microsoft Entra ID for Windows devices
BitLocker key rotation is supported on iOS/iPadOS devices
Bulk device actions can run on up to 100 devices at a time
Bulk wipes do not count toward the daily tenant limit for the wipe action
questions.explanation: Bulk actions cap at 100 devices and rotating the local admin password for Windows requires that Windows LAPS backs up to Microsoft Entra ID. BitLocker key rotation applies to Windows, and bulk wipe, retire, and delete requests do count toward the daily limits.

questions.question: Which two statements about Microsoft Tunnel and Tunnel for MAM are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: Tunnel for MAM on iOS/iPadOS provides device-wide VPN
Tunnel for MAM requires an existing Microsoft Tunnel gateway
Tunnel for MAM supports devices that are not enrolled in Intune
Tunnel for MAM replaces the Microsoft Tunnel gateway
questions.explanation: Tunnel for MAM extends an existing Tunnel gateway to unenrolled devices. It does not replace the gateway, and on iOS/iPadOS it is per-app through the SDK, not device-wide.

questions.question: The security team connected Intune to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. They want Windows laptops that have an active high-severity threat to lose access to Exchange Online until they are cleaned. Which combination does this?
options: A compliance policy requiring a low machine risk score, plus Conditional Access requiring compliant devices
A security baseline for Microsoft Edge applied to the affected laptops
An EDR policy that blocks the Exchange Online URLs on the laptop whenever a threat exists
An app configuration policy that changes Outlook's sign-in settings
questions.explanation: The compliance policy marks a device noncompliant when its risk score from Defender for Endpoint exceeds the limit, and Conditional Access blocks noncompliant devices from Exchange Online. An EDR policy onboards devices and sets telemetry options, it does not gate access. A browser baseline and an Outlook configuration are unrelated.

questions.question: Analysts need to see Windows devices in the Microsoft Defender portal, review alerts, and triage incidents. The devices are managed by Intune and not yet visible there. What should the admin deploy?
options: An EDR policy from endpoint security, after enabling the Defender for Endpoint connector
A Wi-Fi profile that points the devices at the Defender portal address
An app protection policy for the Defender portal website on managed devices
A device restrictions profile that turns off Microsoft Defender Antivirus
questions.explanation: The EDR policy deploys the Defender for Endpoint onboarding configuration, so devices show up in the Defender portal where analysts investigate and triage; the Intune connector must be on first. The other options neither onboard devices nor help analysts, and disabling antivirus is harmful.

questions.question: The security team assigned the Windows 11 version 25H2 baseline last year. Microsoft has released the 26H2 baseline. The admin notices devices still show the old baseline settings. Why?
options: A baseline can be assigned only once per tenant, so the old one blocks the new one
Existing baseline profiles do not update automatically; create a profile on the new version or update it
Microsoft retires the old baseline from devices as soon as a new version exists
The baseline only updates when Windows Update installs the matching Windows feature update
questions.explanation: Intune security baseline profiles stay on the version they were created with, so admins must create a new profile or update to the latest version, ideally testing on a pilot group. Windows feature updates do not change Intune baselines, there is no one-baseline-per-tenant rule, and old baselines are not removed from devices automatically.

questions.question: Which two statements about update management for Apple and Android devices in Intune are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: Apple update policies must use the legacy MDM update commands
Android FOTA applies to personally owned work profile devices
Apple update policies are created in the settings catalog by using Declarative Device Management
Android FOTA is available for corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices and needs Intune Plan 2
questions.explanation: The settings catalog with Declarative Device Management is the current method for iOS/iPadOS and macOS updates, and FOTA covers corporate-owned Android Enterprise devices with a Plan 2 license. The legacy MDM update policies are deprecated, and personally owned work profiles are not included in FOTA.

questions.question: A bank wants Outlook and Teams notifications on managed phones muted every weekday from 18:00 to 07:00 and on weekends, for iOS and Android users, without asking users to change anything. Which feature does this?
options: A compliance policy with a grace period covering working hours
An app protection policy with conditional launch settings for Outlook and Teams
A quiet time policy using the days of the week type
An app configuration policy for the Company Portal app
questions.explanation: Quiet time policies mute Outlook email and Teams notifications on iOS/iPadOS and Android during set periods; the days of the week type supports certain hours or all day on selected days. App protection conditional launch checks risk, compliance grace periods apply to noncompliance, and Company Portal configuration does not mute notifications.

questions.question: The company deploys Microsoft 365 Apps through Intune and wants IT to control which channel each department's Office installation follows, see app health across devices, and manage Office policy settings centrally. Which service should the admin use for this?
options: Windows Update for Business reports in Azure Monitor
The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center, alongside Intune for the deployment
The Microsoft Store app (new) type in Intune
Group Policy analytics in the Intune admin center
questions.explanation: The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center handles servicing profiles, inventory and health, and policy management for the apps, while Intune deploys them. Update reports are about Windows updates, the Store app type is for Store apps, and Group Policy Analytics evaluates GPOs.

questions.question: New Autopilot laptops should have Microsoft 365 Apps installed before the user reaches the desktop. The app is a required assignment to the device group, and it installs successfully a few minutes after sign-in, so users see the desktop with Office still missing. What is the most likely cause?
options: The Microsoft 365 Apps app type cannot be assigned to a device group at all
The Autopilot profile has a device name template set, which delays all app installs
The laptops use a self-deploying profile, which can never install any apps
The Enrollment Status Page is not set to wait for this app as a required app
questions.explanation: The ESP only holds the user at the setup screens until the apps it is configured to track have installed, so the app has to be a required app that the ESP is told to wait for. A name template has no effect on app installs, self-deploying profiles can install apps, and Microsoft 365 Apps can be assigned to device groups.

questions.question: A Win32 app shows as failed on 40 laptops and the user says nothing happened. The admin wants to see per-device status and then pull logs from one affected laptop without disturbing the user. What should be done?
options: Review the app's device install status, then run Collect diagnostics on one device
Delete the app and recreate it from scratch with the same packaging
Switch the assignment from required to available for all of the users
Wipe one laptop and see whether the app installs after re-enrollment
questions.explanation: The app's device install status shows where and why it failed, and Collect diagnostics gathers logs remotely, which avoids disrupting the user. Recreating the app, wiping a device, or changing the assignment hides the cause instead of diagnosing it.

questions.question: Quiet time policies are supported in all Intune clouds, including GCC High and DoD.
questions.explanation: Quiet time policies are not supported in sovereign clouds such as GCC, GCC High, DoD, and Azure operated by 21Vianet.

questions.question: A second administrator must approve every PowerShell script before it runs on devices, and the approvers are overloaded. They want risk-based recommendations about each request inside the approval workflow, while still making the final decision. Which capability helps?
options: A scope tag applied to each script that is submitted
The Device Offboarding Agent, which handles stale devices
The Policy Configuration Agent, which proposes policies from documents
The Change Review Agent in Security Copilot
questions.explanation: The Change Review Agent evaluates Multi Admin Approval requests and recommends actions; approvers still decide. The Device Offboarding Agent deals with stale devices and the Policy Configuration Agent turns documents and baselines into recommended policy. Scope tags control which admins can see objects.

questions.question: The security team wants to prioritize fixing weaknesses on managed devices using Defender vulnerability data, with AI-driven risk assessments, and run the agent under its own non-human identity. Which should the admin set up?
options: The Vulnerability Remediation Agent, using a Microsoft Entra agentic identity
The Change Review Agent, running under a shared administrator account
Copilot Chat prompts that are saved as a custom report in the admin center
The Policy Configuration Agent, using the Global Administrator role
questions.explanation: The Vulnerability Remediation Agent monitors vulnerabilities from Defender data and prioritizes remediation, and it now uses a Microsoft Entra agentic identity rather than a human user identity. The other agents do different jobs, and Copilot Chat prompts do not run autonomous work.

questions.question: An admin has a security standards document written in plain language and wants Intune to propose matching policies and settings to review. Which capability should be used?
options: Windows Update for Business reports
The Policy Configuration Agent
The Device Offboarding Agent
The anomalies report in Advanced Analytics
questions.explanation: The Policy Configuration Agent converts plain-language documents and industry baselines into recommended settings and policies for the admin to review. The Device Offboarding Agent finds stale devices, update reports show update status, and the anomalies report finds device health regressions.

questions.question: After a driver update, several laptops of one model begin crashing apps repeatedly. IT wants Intune to group the affected devices by shared attributes such as driver version and warn about others at risk. Which report helps?
options: The device compliance policy summary page for the affected devices
The enrollment failures report under Devices > Monitor
The Windows Update for Business feature update report for the affected model
The Advanced Analytics anomalies report, using device correlation groups
questions.explanation: The anomalies report detects app hangs, crashes, and stop error restarts after changes and groups affected devices into device correlation groups by attributes such as driver or OS version, flagging at-risk devices. The other reports cover update progress, enrollment, and compliance status.

questions.question: A new tenant shows the Startup performance report with no score and the message insufficient data. Only three enrolled test devices are reporting. What explains this?
options: Endpoint analytics needs at least five reporting devices before it shows a score
Scores only appear after a custom baseline has been configured in the tenant
Endpoint analytics scores require Windows 365 Cloud PCs to be present in the tenant
The All organizations median baseline has not yet been created by the admin
questions.explanation: Endpoint analytics requires at least five reporting devices for a score, otherwise it shows insufficient data. Cloud PCs are not required, and the median baseline is built in.

questions.question: An admin wants to confirm that the Apple Push Notification service certificate and the Apple VPP token will not expire unnoticed. Where can both connectors' health be checked in one place?
options: Endpoint analytics > Startup performance for the Apple devices
Tenant administration > Tenant status, under connector status
Devices > Monitor > Enrollment failures, filtered to Apple devices
Apps > Quiet Time > Policies, which list tokens and certificates
questions.explanation: Tenant status shows connector status for connectors such as APNs certificates and VPP tokens, with warnings seven days before expiry and unhealthy states for expired credentials or stale syncs. The other locations show enrollment failures, device boot performance, and notification policies.

questions.question: The Intune team wants to read upcoming Intune changes and active service incidents that affect their tenant, without leaving the Intune admin center. Which should they use?
options: The Windows Autopatch status report for the tenant
The device compliance report in the Intune admin center
The Collect diagnostics device action on a test device
The service health and message center areas of Tenant status
questions.explanation: The Tenant status page includes service health incidents and the Intune message center with upcoming and recent changes.
